title: Keritot 5
description: Separate lashes for bread, parched grain and fresh stalks before the omer, four sages on verbal analogies that carry “fundamentals of the Torah”, and the anointing oil: its blending, its weights, its miracles, the kings and High Priests anointed with it, and its sequestering with the Ark.
topics: 🌾 Bread, parched grain and fresh stalks: why one is flogged three times before the omer
🔗 “Never regard a verbal analogy lightly”: piggul, notar, a daughter from a woman one raped, and those who are stoned
🫒 Blending the anointing oil and the incense: for oneself, for the community, in halves
⚖️ The weights of the spices, 1,750 shekels, and whether one weighs with a surplus
✨ Twelve log that anointed the Tabernacle, Aaron, High Priests and kings and remain for the future
👑 Which kings were anointed: Solomon, Joash, Jehoahaz, Jehu, and the sons of Josiah
📦 What was sequestered with the Ark, and how kings and priests are anointed
🕯️ Anointing kings by a spring, and Rav Ami’s signs for the year, a business and a journey

a2.he: וַעֲדַיִין, לָאו שֶׁבִּכְלָלוֹת הוּא! אִם כֵּן, נֵימָא קְרָא: ״לֹא תוּכַל לְאׇכְלָם בִּשְׁעָרֶיךָ״, ״מַעְשַׂר דְּגָנְךָ תִּירֹשְׁךָ וְיִצְהָרֶךָ״ לְמָה לִּי? לְיַחוֹדֵי אֲכִילָה דְּכׇל חַד וְחַד.

a3.he: אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק: הָאוֹכֵל לֶחֶם, קָלִי, וְכַרְמֶל – לוֹקֶה שָׁלֹשׁ. וְהָא אֵין לוֹקִין עַל לָאו שֶׁבִּכְלָלוֹת! שָׁאנֵי הָכָא דִּמְיַיתַּר קְרָאֵי –

a4.he: לֵימָא קְרָא לֶחֶם, וְנֵילַף קָלִי וְכַרְמֶל מִינֵּיהּ. אִיכָּא לְמִיפְרַךְ: מָה לְלֶחֶם, שֶׁכֵּן נִתְרַבָּה אֵצֶל חַלָּה!

a5.he: נִכְתּוֹב קָלִי וְלָא לִכְתּוֹב לֶחֶם, וְנֵילַף מִקָּלִי. לֶחֶם מִקָּלִי לָא אָתֵי, מִשּׁוּם דְּקָלֵי אִיתֵיהּ בְּעֵינֵיהּ, לֶחֶם לָא אִיתֵיהּ בְּעֵינֵיהּ. כַּרְמֶל מִקָּלִי לָא אָתֵי, מִשּׁוּם דְּקָלִי נִתְרַבָּה אֵצֶל מְנָחוֹת, כַּרְמֶל לֹא נִתְרַבָּה אֵצֶל מְנָחוֹת!

a6.he: נִכְתּוֹב כַּרְמֶל וְנֵילַף לֶחֶם וְקָלִי מִינֵּיהּ. אִיכָּא לְמִיפְרַךְ: מָה לְכַרְמֶל שֶׁכֵּן לֹא נִשְׁתַּנָּה מִבְּרִיָּיתוֹ! מִן חַד לָא יָלְפִי, נֵילַף חֲדָא מִן תְּרֵין?

a7.he: לָא נִכְתּוֹב קְרָא לֶחֶם וְנֵילַף מִקָּלִי וְכַרְמֶל – אִיכָּא לְמִיפְרַךְ: מָה לְקָלִי וְכַרְמֶל דְּאִיתַנְהוֹן בְּעֵינֵיהוֹן! לָא נִכְתּוֹב קְרָא כַּרְמֶל וְנֵילַף מִלֶּחֶם וְקָלִי – אִיכָּא לְמִיפְרַךְ: מָה לְלֶחֶם וְקָלִי שֶׁכֵּן נִתְרַבּוּ אֵצֶל מְנָחוֹת!

a8.he: אָמַר לָךְ רַבִּי יִצְחָק: לָא נִכְתּוֹב קְרָא קָלִי, וְנֵילַף מִלֶּחֶם וְכַרְמֶל. מַאי פָּרְכַתְּ? אִי פָּרְכַתְּ: מָה לְלֶחֶם, שֶׁכֵּן נִתְרַבָּה אֵצֶל חַלָּה – כַּרְמֶל יוֹכִיחַ! וְאִי מִשּׁוּם דְּכַרְמֶל לֹא נִשְׁתַּנָּה מִבְּרִיָּיתוֹ – לֶחֶם יוֹכִיחַ! הִלְכָּךְ לוֹקֶה, דִּמְיַיתַּר.

a9.he: וְאֵימָא: קָלִי דִּמְיַיתַּר מִחַיַּיב חֲדָא, אַכּוּלְּהוֹן מִחַיַּיב חֲדָא! אִם כֵּן, נִכְתּוֹב קְרָא: ״לֶחֶם כַּרְמֶל וְקָלִי״, אִי נָמֵי נִכְתּוֹב: ״קָלִי וְלֶחֶם וְכַרְמֶל״, אַמַּאי כְּתַב לְקָלִי בָּאֶמְצַע? הָכִי קָאָמַר: לֶחֶם בְּקָלִי נִחַיַּיב וְכַרְמֶל נִחַיַּיב בְּקָלִי.

a10.he: אָמַר רַבִּי יַנַּאי: לְעוֹלָם אַל תְּהִי גְּזֵירָה שָׁוָה קַלָּה בְּעֵינֶיךָ, שֶׁהֲרֵי פִּיגּוּל אֶחָד מִגּוּפֵי תוֹרָה, וְלֹא לִימְּדוֹ הַכָּתוּב אֶלָּא מִגְּזֵירָה שָׁוָה.

a11.he: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן, תָּנֵי זַבְדָּא בַּר לֵוִי: נֶאֱמַר לְהַלָּן: ״וְאוֹכְלָיו עֲוֹנוֹ יִשָּׂא״, וְנֶאֱמַר כָּאן: ״וְהַנֶּפֶשׁ הָאֹכֶלֶת מִמֶּנּוּ עֲוֹנָהּ תִּשָּׂא״, מָה לְהַלָּן כָּרֵת – אַף כָּאן כָּרֵת.

a12.he: אָמַר רַבִּי סִימַאי: לְעוֹלָם אַל תְּהִי גְּזֵירָה שָׁוָה קַלָּה בְּעֵינֶיךָ, שֶׁהֲרֵי נוֹתָר אֶחָד מִגּוּפֵי תוֹרָה, וְלֹא לִימְּדוֹ הַכָּתוּב אֶלָּא מִגְּזֵירָה שָׁוָה.

a13.he: מַאי הִיא? יָלֵיף ״קֹדֶשׁ״ ״קֹדֶשׁ״ – ״וְאוֹכְלָיו עֲוֹנוֹ יִשָּׂא כִּי אֶת קֹדֶשׁ ה׳ חִלֵּל״, וּכְתִיב: ״וְשָׂרַפְתָּ אֶת הַנּוֹתָר בָּאֵשׁ כִּי קֹדֶשׁ וְגוֹ׳״

a14.he: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: לְעוֹלָם אַל תְּהִי גְּזֵירָה שָׁוָה קַלָּה בְּעֵינֶיךָ, שֶׁהֲרֵי בִּתּוֹ מֵאֲנוּסָתוֹ הֵן הֵן גּוּפֵי תוֹרָה, וְלֹא לִימְּדָהּ הַכָּתוּב אֶלָּא מִגְּזֵירָה שָׁוָה.

a15.he: דְּאָמַר רָבָא, אֲמַר לִי רַבִּי יִצְחָק בַּר אַבְדִּימִי: אָתְיָא ״הֵנָּה״ ״הֵנָּה״ לְאִיסּוּרָא,

a17.he: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: אַל תְּהִי גְּזֵירָה שָׁוָה קַלָּה בְּעֵינֶיךָ, שֶׁהֲרֵי נִסְקָלִים הֵן הֵן גּוּפֵי תוֹרָה, וְלֹא לִימְּדָהּ הַכָּתוּב אֶלָּא מִגְּזֵירָה שָׁוָה,

a18.he: דְּתַנְיָא: נֶאֱמַר כָּאן: ״דְּמֵיהֶם בָּם״ וְנֶאֱמַר בְּאוֹב וְיִדְּעוֹנִי: ״דְּמֵיהֶם בָּם״. מָה לְהַלָּן – בִּסְקִילָה, אַף כָּאן – בִּסְקִילָה.

a19.he: הַמְּפַטֵּם אֶת הַשֶּׁמֶן כּוּ׳. תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: הַמְּפַטֵּם אֶת הַשֶּׁמֶן לִלְמוֹד בּוֹ, לְמוֹסְרוֹ לַצִּיבּוּר – פָּטוּר, לָסוּךְ – חַיָּיב. וְהַסָּךְ מִמֶּנּוּ – פָּטוּר, לְפִי שֶׁאֵין חַיָּיבִין אֶלָּא עַל סִיכַת שֶׁמֶן הַמִּשְׁחָה שֶׁעָשָׂה מֹשֶׁה בִּלְבַד.

a20.he: אָמַר מָר: לִלְמוֹד בּוֹ עַל מְנָת לְמוֹסְרוֹ לַצִּיבּוּר – פָּטוּר. מְנָלַן? אַתְיָא ״מַתְכֻּנְתּוֹ״ מִן ״בְּמַתְכּוּנְתָּהּ״ דִּקְטֹרֶת, וּכְתִיב לְגַבֵּי קְטֹרֶת: ״לֹא תַעֲשׂוּ לָכֶם״ – לָכֶם הוּא דְּאָסוּר, אֲבָל לְמוֹסְרוֹ לַצִּיבּוּר – פָּטוּר, גַּבֵּי שֶׁמֶן נָמֵי, לְמוֹסְרוֹ לַצִּיבּוּר – פָּטוּר.

a21.he: וְתִיהְדַּר קְטֹרֶת וְנֵילַף מִשֶּׁמֶן: מָה שֶׁמֶן כִּי מְפַטֵּם לַחֲצָיִין – פָּטוּר, אַף קְטֹרֶת נָמֵי כִּי מְפַטֵּם לַחֲצָיִין – פָּטוּר! אַלְּמָה אָמַר רָבָא: קְטֹרֶת שֶׁפִּטְּמָהּ לַחֲצָיִין – חַיָּיב, שֶׁמֶן שֶׁפִּטְּמוֹ לַחֲצָיִין – פָּטוּר?

a22.he: אָמַר לָךְ רָבָא: גַּבֵּי שֶׁמֶן כְּתִיב ״וּבְמַתְכֻּנְתּוֹ לֹא תַעֲשׂוּ כָּמוֹהוּ״ – כָּמוֹהוּ הוּא דְּאָסוּר, אֲבָל חֶצְיוֹ שַׁפִּיר דָּמֵי. גַּבֵּי קְטֹרֶת דִּכְתִיב ״וְהַקְּטֹרֶת אֲשֶׁר תַּעֲשֶׂה״ – כֹּל עֲשִׂיָּיה דִקְטֹרֶת אֶפְשָׁר דְּמַקְטֵיר פְּרָס שַׁחֲרִית וּפְרָס בֵּין הָעַרְבַּיִם.

a23.he: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: שֶׁמֶן הַמִּשְׁחָה מׇר דְּרוֹר חֲמֵשׁ מֵאוֹת, קִדָּה חֲמֵשׁ מֵאוֹת, קִנְּמָן בֶּשֶׂם חֲמֵשׁ מֵאוֹת, וּקְנֵה בֹשֶׂם חֲמִשִּׁים וּמָאתָיִם, נִמְצְאוּ כּוּלָּם אֶלֶף וְשִׁבְעָה מֵאוֹת וַחֲמִשִּׁים.

a24.he: תַּנָּא מִנְיָינָא קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן? תַּנָּא הָא קָא קַשְׁיָא לֵיהּ, אֵימָא: קְנֵה בֹשֶׂם כְּקִנְּמׇן בֶּשֶׂם, מָה קִנְּמׇן בֶּשֶׂם מַחֲצִיתוֹ בַּחֲמִשִּׁים וּמָאתַיִם – אַף קְנֵה בֹשֶׂם מַחֲצִיתוֹ חֲמִשִּׁים וּמָאתָיִם, דְּהָווּ לְהוּ תְּרֵין אֲלָפִים.

a25.he: וְאֵימָא הָכִי נָמֵי! אִם כֵּן, נִכְתּוֹב קְרָא: ״קִנְּמׇן בֶּשֶׂם וּקְנֵה בֹשֶׂם מֶחֱצָה וּמֶחֱצָה חֲמִשִּׁים וּמָאתַיִם״.

a26.he: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב פָּפָּא לְאַבָּיֵי: כְּשֶׁהוּא שׁוֹקֵל, בְּהֶכְרֵעַ הוּא שׁוֹקֵל, אוֹ עַיִן בְּעַיִן הוּא שׁוֹקֵל? אֲמַר לֵיהּ: רַחֲמָנָא כְּתַב: ״בַּד בְּבַד״, וְאַתְּ אָמְרַתְּ בְּהֶכְרֵעַ? וְהָאָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה: הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא יוֹדֵעַ הַכְרָעוֹת, אַלְמָא דְּאִית בְּהוּ הֶכְרֵעַ!

a27.he: אֶלָּא, אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה: דְּקִנְּמׇן בֶּשֶׂם אַמַּאי מַיְיתֵי מַחֲצִיתוֹ דַּחֲמֵשׁ מֵאוֹת, חֲמִשִּׁים וּמָאתַיִם בְּחַד זִימְנָא וַחֲמִשִּׁים וּמָאתַיִם בְּחַד זִימְנָא? כֵּיוָן דְּכוּלְּהוֹן חֲמֵשׁ מֵאוֹת הָוַיִין, נַיְיתֵי חֲמֵשׁ מֵאוֹת בְּבַת אַחַת! שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ, מִדְּקָמַיְיתֵי לַהּ לְקִנְּמׇן בֶּשֶׂם בִּתְרֵי זִימְנֵי, הֶכְרֵעַ אִית בֵּיהּ, וְהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא יוֹדֵעַ בְּהֶכְרֵעוֹת.

a28.he: וּמַאי ״בַּד בְּבַד״? אָמַר רָבִינָא: שֶׁלֹּא יַנִּיחַ מִשְׁקָל בְּמִשְׁקָל וְיִשְׁקוֹל.

a29.he: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: שֶׁמֶן הַמִּשְׁחָה שֶׁעָשָׂה מֹשֶׁה בְמִדְבַּר – מְשַׁלְּקוֹ הָעִיקָּרִין, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי יְהוּדָה. אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי יוֹסֵי: וַהֲלֹא לָסוּךְ הָעִיקָּרִין אֵינוֹ סִיפֵּק! כֵּיצַד עוֹשֶׂה? הֵבִיאוּ הָעִיקָּרִין וּשְׁלָקוּם בְּמַיִם, וְהֵצִיף עֲלֵיהֶן שֶׁמֶן הַמִּשְׁחָה, וְקָלַט אֶת הָרֵיחַ, וְקִיפְּחוֹ.

b1.he: וְכִי נֵס אֶחָד נַעֲשָׂה בַּשֶּׁמֶן הַמִּשְׁחָה? וַהֲלֹא נִסִּים הַרְבֵּה נַעֲשׂוּ בּוֹ מִתְּחִלָּתוֹ וְעַד סוֹפוֹ, תְּחִלָּתוֹ לֹא הָיָה אֶלָּא שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר לוֹג, וּבוֹ נִמְשַׁח הַמִּשְׁכָּן וְכֵלָיו וְאַהֲרֹן וּבָנָיו כׇּל שִׁבְעַת יְמֵי הַמִּלּוּאִים, וּבוֹ נִמְשְׁחוּ כֹּהֲנִים גְּדוֹלִים וּמְלָכִים, וְכוּלּוֹ קַיָּים לֶעָתִיד לָבֹא,

b2.he: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״שֶׁמֶן מִשְׁחַת קֹדֶשׁ יִהְיֶה זֶה לִי לְדֹרֹתֵיכֶם״ – ״זֶה״ בְּגִימַטְרִיָּא שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר לוּגִּין הָוְיָין.

b3.he: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן ״וַיִּקַּח מֹשֶׁה אֶת שֶׁמֶן הַמִּשְׁחָה וַיִּמְשַׁח אֶת הַמִּשְׁכָּן וְגוֹ׳״, רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: שֶׁמֶן הַמִּשְׁחָה שֶׁעָשָׂה מֹשֶׁה בַּמִּדְבָּר הַרְבֵּה נִסִּים נַעֲשׂוּ בּוֹ מִתְּחִלָּתוֹ וְעַד סוֹפוֹ: תְּחִלָּתוֹ לֹא הָיָה אֶלָּא שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר לוּגִּין, כַּמָּה יוֹרָה בּוֹלַעַת, כַּמָּה עִיקָּרִין בּוֹלְעִין, כַּמָּה הָאוּר שׂוֹרֵף, וּבוֹ נִמְשַׁח מִשְׁכָּן וְכֵלָיו, אַהֲרֹן וּבָנָיו כָּל שִׁבְעַת יְמֵי הַמְּלוּאִים,

b4.he: וּבוֹ נִמְשְׁחוּ כֹּהֲנִים גְּדוֹלִים וּמְלָכִים. וַאֲפִילּוּ כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל בֶּן כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל טָעוּן מְשִׁיחָה. וְאֵין מוֹשְׁחִין מֶלֶךְ בֶּן מֶלֶךְ. וְאֵם תֹּאמַר: מִפְּנֵי מָה מָשְׁחוּ אֶת שְׁלֹמֹה? מִפְּנֵי מַחְלוֹקֶת אֲדוֹנִיָּה, וְאֶת יְהוֹאָשׁ – מִפְּנֵי עֲתַלְיָה, וְאֶת יְהוֹאָחָז – מִפְּנֵי יְהוֹיָקִים אָחִיו, שֶׁהָיָה גָּדוֹל מֵאֶחָיו שְׁתֵּי שָׁנִים.

b5.he: אָמַר מָר: וַאֲפִילּוּ כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל בֵּן כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל טָעוּן מְשִׁיחָה. מְנָלַן? דִּכְתִיב: ״וְהַכֹּהֵן הַמָּשִׁיחַ תַּחְתָּיו מִבָּנָיו״, נֵימָא קְרָא ״וְהַכֹּהֵן שֶׁתַּחְתָּיו מִבָּנָיו״, מַאי ״הַמָּשִׁיחַ״? הָא קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן דַּאֲפִילּוּ מִבָּנָיו, הָהוּא דִּמְשַׁח הָוֵי כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל, וְאִי לָא מְשַׁח לָא הָוֵי כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל.

b6.he: אָמַר מָר: אֵין מוֹשְׁחִין מֶלֶךְ בֶּן מֶלֶךְ. מְנָלַן? אָמַר רַב אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב, דִּכְתִיב: ״לְמַעַן יַאֲרִיךְ יָמִים עַל מַמְלַכְתּוֹ הוּא וּבָנָיו כׇּל הַיָּמִים״ – יְרוּשָּׁה הִיא.

b7.he: וּמִפְּנֵי מָה מָשְׁחוּ אֶת שְׁלֹמֹה? מִפְּנֵי מַחְלוֹקֶת אֲדוֹנִיָּה. מְנָלַן דְּכִי אָתֵי מַחְלוֹקֶת בָּעֵי מְשִׁיחָה, וְלָא כׇּל דְּבָעֵי מַלְכָּא מוֹרֵית לֵיהּ מַלְכוּתָא? אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא, אָמַר קְרָא: ״בְּקֶרֶב יִשְׂרָאֵל״ – בִּזְמַן שֶׁשָּׁלוֹם בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל.

b8.he: תָּנָא: אַף יֵהוּא בֶּן נִמְשִׁי לֹא נִמְשַׁח אֶלָּא מִפְּנֵי מַחְלוֹקֶת יוֹרָם בֶּן אַחְאָב: אַמַּאי? תִּיפּוֹק לֵיהּ דְּמֶלֶךְ רִאשׁוֹן הוּא! חַסּוֹרֵי מִיחַסְּרָא וְהָכִי קָתָנֵי: מַלְכֵי בֵּית דָּוִד מוֹשְׁחִין, מַלְכֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל אֵין מוֹשְׁחִין. וְאִם תֹּאמַר: מִפְּנֵי מָה מָשְׁחוּ יֵהוּא בֶּן נִמְשִׁי? מִפְּנֵי מַחְלוֹקֶת יוֹרָם בֶּן אַחְאָב.

b9.he: אָמַר מָר: מַלְכֵי בֵּית דָּוִד מוֹשְׁחִין, וְאֵין מַלְכֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל מוֹשְׁחִין. מְנָלַן? דִּכְתִיב: ״קוּם מְשָׁחֵהוּ כִּי זֶה הוּא״ – זֶה טָעוּן מְשִׁיחָה, וְאֵין אַחֵר טָעוּן מְשִׁיחָה.

b10.he: אָמַר מָר: מִפְּנֵי מַחְלוֹקֶת יוֹרָם. וּמִשּׁוּם מַחְלוֹקֶת יוֹרָם בֶּן אַחְאָב נִמְעַל בְּשֶׁמֶן הַמִּשְׁחָה? כִּדְאָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: בַּאֲפַרְסְמָא דַּכְיָא, הָכָא נָמֵי בַּאֲפַרְסְמָא דַּכְיָא.

b11.he: וְאֶת יְהוֹאָחָז מִפְּנֵי יְהוֹיָקִים, שֶׁהָיָה גָּדוֹל מִמֶּנּוּ שְׁתֵּי שָׁנִים. וּמִי קַשִּׁישׁ? וְהָכְתִיב: ״וּבְנֵי יֹאשִׁיָּה הַבְּכוֹר יוֹחָנָן וְהַשֵּׁנִי יְהוֹיָקִים וְהַשְּׁלִישִׁי צִדְקִיָּהוּ וְהָרְבִיעִי שַׁלּוּם״, וְאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: הוּא יְהוֹאָחָז, הוּא צִדְקִיָּהוּ, הוּא שַׁלּוּם!

b12.he: אֶלָּא לְעוֹלָם יְהוֹיָקִים קַשִּׁישׁ, וְאַמַּאי קָרֵי לֵיהּ בְּכוֹר – שֶׁהוּא בְּכוֹר לַמַּלְכוּת. וּמִי מוֹקְמִינַן זוּטָא קַמֵּי קַשִּׁישָׁא? וְהָכְתִיב: ״וְאֶת הַמַּמְלָכָה נָתַן לִיהוֹרָם כִּי הוּא הַבְּכוֹר״! הַהוּא מְמַלֵּא מְקוֹם אֲבוֹתָיו הֲוָה.

b13.he: אָמַר מָר: הוּא שַׁלּוּם הוּא צִדְקִיָּה. וְהָא בְּדָרֵי קָחָשֵׁיב! וּמַאי קָרֵי לֵיהּ שְׁלִישִׁי? שֶׁהוּא שְׁלִישִׁי לַבָּנִים, וּמַאי קָרֵי לֵיהּ רְבִיעִי? שֶׁהוּא רְבִיעִי לַמַּלְכוּת, מִשּׁוּם דִּמְלַךְ יְכָנְיָה קַמֵּיהּ – בִּתְחִלָּה מְלַךְ יְהוֹאָחָז, וְסוֹף מְלַךְ יְהוֹיָקִים, וְסוֹף מְלַךְ יְכָנְיָה, וְסוֹף מְלַךְ צִדְקִיָּה.

b14.he: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: הוּא שַׁלּוּם הוּא צִדְקִיָּה, וְלָמָּה נִקְרָא שְׁמוֹ שַׁלּוּם? שֶׁהָיָה שָׁלֵם בְּמַעֲשָׂיו. דָּבָר אַחֵר: שַׁלּוּם – שֶׁשָּׁלֵם מַלְכוּת בֵּית דָּוִד בְּיָמָיו, וּמָה שְׁמוֹ? מַתַּנְיָה שְׁמוֹ, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״וַיַּמְלֵךְ אֶת מַתַּנְיָה דֹדוֹ תַּחְתָּיו וַיַּסֵּב שְׁמוֹ צִדְקִיָּה״,

b15.he: דְּאָמַר: לוֹ יָהּ יַצְדִּיק עָלֶיךָ אֶת הַדִּין אִם תִּמְרוֹד בִּי, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״וַיְבִיאֵהוּ בָבֶלָה״ וּכְתִיב: ״וְגַם בַּמֶּלֶךְ נְבוּכַד נֶאצַּר מֶלֶךְ בָּבֶל מָרָד אֲשֶׁר הִשְׁבִּיעוֹ בֵּאלֹהִים״.

b16.he: וּמִי הֲוָה שֶׁמֶן הַמִּשְׁחָה? וְהָתַנְיָא: מִשֶּׁנִּגְנַז אָרוֹן נִגְנַז צִנְצֶנֶת הַמָּן, וּצְלוֹחִית שֶׁמֶן הַמִּשְׁחָה, וּמַקְלוֹ שֶׁל אַהֲרֹן שְׁקֵדִים וּפְרָחִים,

b17.he: וְאַרְגַּז שֶׁשִּׁגְּרוּ פְּלִשְׁתִּים דּוֹרוֹן לֵאלֹהֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״וְאֶת כְּלֵי הַזָּהָב אֲשֶׁר הֲשֵׁבֹתֶם לוֹ אָשָׁם תָּשִׂימוּ בָאַרְגַּז מִצִּדּוֹ״. וּמִי גְּנָזוֹ? יֹאשִׁיָּה מֶלֶךְ יְהוּדָה גְּנָזוֹ, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״וַיֹּאמֶר הַמֶּלֶךְ אֶל הַכֹּהֲנִים תְּנוּ אֶת אֲרוֹן הַקֹּדֶשׁ״,

b20.he: אַתְיָא ״מִשְׁמֶרֶת״ ״מִשְׁמֶרֶת״. אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: בַּאֲפַרְסְמָא דַּכְיָא.

b21.he: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: מוֹשְׁחִין אֶת הַמְּלָכִים כְּמִין נֵזֶר, וְאֶת הַכֹּהֲנִים כְּמִין ״כִּי״. אָמַר רַב מְנַשְּׁיָה: כְּמִין ״כִּי״ יְוָנִי. תָּנֵי חֲדָא: בַּתְּחִלָּה מַצִּיק שֶׁמֶן עַל רֹאשׁוֹ וְאַחַר כָּךְ נוֹתֵן לוֹ שֶׁמֶן בֵּין רִיסֵי עֵינָיו, וְתָנֵי אַחֲרִיתִי: בַּתְּחִלָּה נוֹתֵן לוֹ שֶׁמֶן בֵּין רִיסֵי עֵינָיו וְאַחַר כָּךְ מַצִּיק לוֹ שֶׁמֶן עַל רֹאשׁוֹ!

b22.he: תַּנָּאֵי הִיא, אִיכָּא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר מְשִׁיחָה עֲדִיפָא, וְאִיכָּא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר יְצִיקָה עֲדִיפָא. מַאי טַעְמָא דְּמַאן דְּאָמַר יְצִיקָה עֲדִיפָא – שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״וַיִּצֹק מִשֶּׁמֶן הַמִּשְׁחָה עַל רֹאשׁ אַהֲרֹן״, וּמַאן דְּאָמַר מְשִׁיחָה עֲדִיפָא – קָסָבַר: שֶׁכֵּן נִתְרַבָּה אֵצֶל כְּלֵי שָׁרֵת.

b23.he: וְהָכְתִיב: ״וַיִּצֹק״ וּלְבַסּוֹף ״וַיִּמְשַׁח״! הָכִי קָאָמַר: מָה טַעַם ״וַיִּצֹק״ – מִשּׁוּם ״וַיִּמְשַׁח אוֹתוֹ לְקַדְּשׁוֹ״.

b24.he: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: ״כַּשֶּׁמֶן הַטּוֹב הַיּוֹרֵד עַל הָרֹאשׁ וְגוֹ׳״ – כְּמִין שְׁתֵּי טִיפִּין מַרְגָּלִיּוֹת הָיוּ תְּלוּיוֹת לְאַהֲרֹן בִּזְקָנוֹ. אָמַר רַב כָּהֲנָא, תָּנָא: כְּשֶׁהוּא מְסַפֵּר עוֹלוֹת וְיוֹשְׁבוֹת בְּעִיקָּרֵי זְקָנוֹ. וְעַל דָּבָר זֶה הָיָה מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ דּוֹאֵג, שֶׁמָּא חַס וְשָׁלוֹם מָעַלְתִּי בְּשֶׁמֶן הַמִּשְׁחָה.

b25.he: יָצְתָה בַּת קוֹל וְאָמְרָה: ״כְּטַל חֶרְמוֹן שֶׁיֹּרֵד עַל הַרְרֵי צִיּוֹן״, מָה טַל אֵין בּוֹ מְעִילָה – אַף שֶׁמֶן שֶׁיּוֹרֵד עַל זְקַן אַהֲרֹן אֵין בּוֹ מְעִילָה.

b26.he: וַעֲדַיִין אַהֲרֹן הָיָה דּוֹאֵג, שֶׁמָּא מֹשֶׁה לֹא מָעַל, וַאֲנִי מָעַלְתִּי! יָצְתָה בַּת קוֹל וְאָמְרָה לוֹ: ״הִנֵּה מַה טּוֹב וּמַה נָּעִים שֶׁבֶת אַחִים גַּם יָחַד״, מָה מֹשֶׁה לֹא מָעַל, אַף אַתָּה לֹא מָעַלְתָּ.

b27.he: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: אֵין מוֹשְׁחִין אֶת הַמְּלָכִים אֶלָּא עַל הַמַּעְיָין, כְּדֵי שֶׁתִּימָּשֵׁךְ מַלְכוּתָן, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״וַיֹּאמֶר הַמֶּלֶךְ אֶל בְּנָיָהוּ וְגוֹ׳ וְהוֹרַדְתֶּם אֹתוֹ עַל גִּחוֹן וְגוֹ׳ וּמָשַׁח אוֹתוֹ שָׁם״.

b28.he: אָמַר רַב אַמֵּי: הַאי מַאן דְּבָעֵי לִידַּע אִי מָשְׁכָא שַׁתָּא אִי לָא, מַיְיתֵי שְׁרָגָא בְּהָלֵין עַשְׂרָה יוֹמִין דְּבֵין רֵישׁ שַׁתָּא לְיוֹמָא דְכִיפּוּרֵי, וְנִיתְלֵי בְּבֵיתָא דְּלָא נָשֵׁיב זִיקָא, אִי מְשִׁיךְ נְהוֹרֵיהּ נִידַּע דְּמַסֵּיק שַׁתֵּיהּ.

b29.he: וּמַאן דְּבָעֵי נַעֲבֵיד עִיסְקֵי, וּבָעֵי דְּנִידַּע אִי מַצְלַח עִיסְקֵיהּ אִי לָא, נִירַבֵּי תַּרְנְגוֹלָא, אִי שָׁמֵין וְשָׁפַר נִידַּע דְּמַצְלַח.

b30.he: הַאי מַאן דְּבָעֵי נִיפּוֹק בְּאוֹרְחָא, וּבָעֵי דְּנִידַּע אִי הָדַר לְבֵיתֵיהּ – נִיעוֹל נֵיקוּם בְּבֵיתָא דְּבַהֲתָא, אִם חָזֵי

messages.text: 5a

Continued from 4b: Rabbi Illa ruled that one who eats second-tithe grain, wine and oil outside Jerusalem is flogged three times, and the Gemara was explaining why the verse “You may not eat within your gates” is needed.
… reason that the Merciful One writes: “You may not eat” (Deuteronomy 12:17), to establish the consumption of second-tithe produce outside Jerusalem as a prohibition.

verse.he: לֹא־תוּכַל לֶאֱכֹל בִּשְׁעָרֶיךָ מַעְשַׂר דְּגָנְךָ וְתִירֹשְׁךָ וְיִצְהָרֶךָ וּבְכֹרֹת בְּקָרְךָ וְצֹאנֶךָ וְכׇל־נְדָרֶיךָ אֲשֶׁר תִּדֹּר וְנִדְבֹתֶיךָ וּתְרוּמַת יָדֶךָ׃
verse.en: You may not partake in your settlements of the tithes of your new grain or wine or oil, or of the firstlings of your herds and flocks, or of any of the votive offerings that you vow, or of your freewill offerings, or of your contributions.

messages.text: The Gemara challenges: But still, it is a general prohibition, as all three types of second tithe are included in a single command.

notes.he: אמאי לקי לאו שבכללות הוא ולאו לחלק:
notes.en: [Editor’s note: up to here belongs to 4b.] And still: why is he flogged? It is a general prohibition, and [the verse is] not for dividing [the prohibitions].

messages.text: The Gemara explains: If so, that one receives only one set of lashes, let the verse say: You may not eat them within your gates, as a previous verse already stated “your tithes” (Deuteronomy 12:11). Why do I need the verse to specify: “The tithe of your grain, of your wine, and of your oil”? This serves to designate a prohibition and the punishment of lashes for the consumption of each and every type of produce.

notes.he: דהא איירי לעיל עולותיכם וזבחיכם מעשרותיכם וגו':
notes.en: Let it write “You may not eat them”: since above [the passage] already spoke of “your burnt offerings and your sacrifices, your tithes,” etc. [Deuteronomy 12:6].

notes.dh: א"כ לכתוב קרא לא תוכל לאכלם
notes.he: ולא מצי למימר מדהוי ליה למימר דגנך לחוד דאכל חד וחד איכא פירכא דגן שנתרבה אצל חלה ותירוש בנסכים ויצהר במנחות ל"א ומתירוש ויצהר לא אתי דגן שכן יש בהן צד ריבוי אצל מזבח אך קשה דליכתוב דגן ויצהר או דגן ותירוש וליתי הך מינייהו:
notes.en: If so, let the verse write “You may not eat them”: and [the Gemara] could not say [the extra wording is] because it should have said only “your grain,” [and then derived wine and oil from it, so that the full list shows] one [is flogged] for each one separately. For there is a refutation: grain was increased with regard to ḥalla, wine with libations, and oil with meal offerings; and grain cannot be derived from wine and oil, since they have an aspect of increase with regard to the altar. But it is difficult: let it write grain and oil, or grain and wine, and derive the remaining one from them.

notes.he: א"כ דמשום לאו שבכללות גרידא נימא קרא לא תוכל לאכלם שכבר הזכירן:
notes.en: If so: that it is merely for the sake of a general prohibition, let the verse say “You may not eat them,” since it already mentioned them.

messages.text: One who eats bread, parched grain, and fresh stalks before the omer offering has been sacrificed is flogged with three sets of lashes, as it states: “And you shall eat neither bread, nor parched grain, nor fresh stalks until this day itself, until you have brought the offering of your God; it is a statute forever throughout your generations in all your dwellings” (Leviticus 23:14).

verse.he: וְלֶחֶם וְקָלִי וְכַרְמֶל לֹא תֹאכְלוּ עַד־עֶצֶם הַיּוֹם הַזֶּה עַד הֲבִיאֲכֶם אֶת־קׇרְבַּן אֱלֹהֵיכֶם חֻקַּת עוֹלָם לְדֹרֹתֵיכֶם בְּכֹל מֹשְׁבֹתֵיכֶם׃ {ס}
verse.en: Until that very day, until you have brought the offering of your God, you shall eat no bread or parched grain or fresh ears; it is a law for all time throughout the ages in all your settlements.

notes.he: לפני העומר:
notes.en: Bread, parched grain and fresh stalks: before the omer.

notes.he: שנתייבש בתנור:
notes.en: Parched grain [kali]: that was dried in an oven.

notes.he: שנתמולל ביד ולא הובהב באור:
notes.en: Fresh stalks [karmel]: that was rubbed by hand and not singed in the fire.

notes.he: קודם העומר:
notes.en: Bread, parched grain and fresh stalks: before the omer.

messages.text: The Gemara raises a difficulty: But one is not flogged for transgressing a general prohibition. The Gemara answers: It is different here, as the verses are superfluous; the verse did not need to specify these three types of grain products.
messages.quote: is flogged with three sets of lashes

messages.text: The Gemara tries to ascertain which terms are superfluous. Let the verse say “bread,” and we will derive the halakha of parched grain and fresh stalks from that of bread.

This derivation can be refuted: What is unique about bread? It is unique in that it has an increased obligation with regard to ḥalla, which is separated only from the dough of bread, not from parched grain and fresh stalks not made into dough.
The Gemara further suggests: Let the verse write only “parched grain,” and let it not write bread or fresh stalks, and we will derive the halakha of bread and fresh stalks from that of parched grain.

The halakha of bread cannot be derived from that of parched grain due to the fact that parched grain is in its unadulterated form, whereas bread is not in its unadulterated form, i.e., it has been fully processed, and therefore it can be maintained that only produce that has not been changed is prohibited before the omer.

notes.he: קלי וכרמל איתנהו בעינייהו דלא טחנן:
notes.en: Parched grain and fresh stalks are in their unadulterated form, since they are not ground.

notes.he: דלא נטחן ולא נתערב במים ומלח:
notes.en: That parched grain is in its unadulterated form: that it was not ground and not mixed with water and salt.

messages.text: Likewise, the halakha of fresh stalks cannot be derived from that of parched grain due to the fact that parched grain has an increased obligation with regard to meal offerings, as the omer meal offering is of parched grain, whereas fresh stalks do not have an increased obligation with regard to meal offerings.

notes.he: במנחת העומר דכתיב גביה (ויקרא ב) קלוי באש ואף על גב דבההוא קרא כתיב כרמל לא הוכשר אלא על ידי האור כדאמרינן במנחות (דף סו:) אבוב של קליות היה שם מנוקב ככברה שיהא האור שולט בכולן ולשון כרמל רך ומל רך שנמלל:
notes.en: Parched grain was increased: in the omer meal offering, as it is written concerning it (Leviticus 2[:14]): “parched with fire.” And although karmel is written in that verse, it was made fit only by means of the fire, as we say in Menaḥot (66b): there was a tube for parched grain there, perforated like a sieve, so that the fire would reach all of it. And the word karmel means rakh u-mal, soft and rubbed: soft, that was rubbed.

notes.he: אביב קלוי באש גרש כרמל האי כרמל היינו רך ומל כדמתרגם פירוכן רכיכן:
notes.en: That parched grain was increased with regard to meal offerings: “Ears of grain parched with fire, groats of karmel” [Leviticus 2:14]. This karmel is rakh u-mal, soft and rubbed, as the Targum renders it: perukhan rekhikhan, soft groats.

notes.he: כרמל לא נתרבה אצל מנחות דהאי כרמל דלא תאכלו היינו יבש לגמרי כדמתרגם לחם וקלי ופירוכן ולא כתב ביה רכיכן:
notes.en: Fresh stalks were not increased with regard to meal offerings, since this karmel of “you shall not eat” is completely dry, as the Targum renders: “bread and parched grain and perukhan,” and does not write rekhikhan [soft] of it.

messages.text: The Gemara further suggests: Let the verse write only “fresh stalks,” and we will derive the halakha of bread and parched grain from that of fresh stalks. This derivation can be refuted: What is unique about fresh stalks? They are unique in that they have not changed from their original state at all.

notes.he: כלל שלא נתחרך ולא נטחן:
notes.en: What about fresh stalks, which have not changed from their original state: at all, for it was not roasted and not ground.

messages.text: Clearly, the halakha of two of these types cannot be derived from the halakha of any one of the others. But let us derive the halakha of one of them from the halakha of the other two.

notes.he: לחם ישנו במנחות דלחם הפנים איקרי מנחה ושתי הלחם של עצרת דכתיב בהו (במדבר כח) בהקריבכם מנחה חדשה:
notes.en: Bread is found among meal offerings, since the shewbread is called a meal offering, and [so are] the two loaves of Shavuot, of which it is written (Numbers 28[:26]): “When you bring a new meal offering.”

messages.text: Let the verse not write bread, and let us derive its halakha from that of parched grain and fresh stalks. This derivation can be refuted: What is unique about parched grain and fresh stalks? They are unique in that relative to bread, which has been fully processed, they are in their unadulterated form.

notes.he: הלכך לא מצית ילפת לה דהא כי אמרינן מה לקלי דאיתיה בעיניה ליכא למימר כרמל יוכיח:
notes.en: Since they are in their unadulterated form: therefore you cannot derive it [bread from them], for when we say, “What about parched grain, which is in its unadulterated form?” one cannot say, “Fresh stalks will prove it.”

notes.he: שכן איתנהון בעיניהון דלא נטחן ולא נתערבו במים ומלח:
notes.en: What about parched grain and fresh stalks: since they are in their unadulterated form, for they were not ground and not mixed with water and salt.

messages.text: Let the verse not write fresh stalks, and let us derive its halakha from the halakha of bread and parched grain. This derivation can be refuted: What is unique about bread and parched grain? They are unique in that they have an increased obligation with regard to meal offerings.

notes.he: וכי פרכת מה לקלי שכן נתרבה על ידי מנחות ליכא למימר לחם יוכיח:
notes.en: Since they were increased with regard to meal offerings: and when you refute, “What about parched grain, which was increased by way of meal offerings?” one cannot say, “Bread will prove it.”

messages.text: Rabbi Yitzḥak could say to you: Let the verse not write parched grain, and let us derive its halakha from the halakha of bread and fresh stalks. What would you say to refute this?

If you refute it by saying: What is unique about bread? It is unique in that it has an increased obligation with regard to ḥalla, the example of fresh stalks will prove that this is not a decisive factor, as the obligation of ḥalla does not apply to it and yet it is prohibited before the omer.

And if you would refute the derivation due to the fact that fresh stalks differ from parched grain, as they have not changed from their original state, the case of bread will prove that this is not the key factor, as it has changed from its original state and yet it is prohibited. Therefore, one is flogged for each type, as the verse is superfluous.

notes.he: קלי מייתר דלא נכתוב קלי ואי פרכת דכרמל דלא נשתנה מברייתו אפי' ע"י חירוך לחם יוכיח:
notes.en: Rabbi Yitzḥak could say to you: parched grain is superfluous, [so that the verse] need not write parched grain. And if you refute: [what about] fresh stalks, which have not changed from their original state, even by roasting? Bread will prove it.

messages.text: The Gemara objects: But why not say that for the consumption of parched grain, whose mention is superfluous, one is separately liable to receive one set of lashes, whereas for eating all the rest of them, i.e., bread and fresh stalks, one is liable to be flogged with only one set of lashes, as they are prohibited by a general prohibition?

notes.dh: אימא קלי דמייתר נחייב חדא וכו'
notes.he: לעיל גבי חלב שור וכבש ועז הוי מצי למיפרך הכי:
notes.en: But say that for parched grain, which is superfluous, one is liable once, etc.: above, concerning the fat of an ox, a sheep and a goat, [the Gemara] could have raised the same challenge.

messages.text: If so, and the halakha of parched grain is unique, let the verse write: Bread, fresh stalks, and parched grain; alternatively, let it write: Parched grain, bread, and fresh stalks. Why does it write the example of parched grain in between the others? This is what the verse is saying: One who eats bread is liable to receive the punishment given for eating parched grain, and likewise one who eats fresh stalks is liable to receive the punishment given for eating parched grain.

notes.he: לחייב מלקות אמאי כתביה קלי במיצעי בין לחם לכרמל הכי קאמר לחם כי קלי נתחייב כרמל כי קלי נתחייב לחייב על כל אחת:
notes.en: Therefore parched grain is superfluous: to obligate lashes. Why did it write parched grain in the middle, between bread and fresh stalks? This is what it is saying: bread, like parched grain, he is liable; fresh stalks, like parched grain, he is liable: to obligate [lashes] for each one.

messages.caption: Bread, parched grain and fresh stalks: what sets each apart, and which derivations of one from the other two are refuted.

messages.text: A verbal analogy should never be lightly regarded in your eyes, as the fact that one is punished with karet for consuming meat of an offering that was sacrificed with the intent to consume it after its appointed time [piggul] is one of the fundamental principles of the Torah, and the verse taught it only through a verbal analogy.

notes.he: דחייבין עליו כרת ולא למדוה הכתוב שיהא בכרת אלא נאמר בקדושים תהיו ואוכליו עונו ישא ואע"ג דכתיב ביה פגול לא בפיגול גמור קמיירי אלא במחשב בשחיטה חוץ למקומו דהכי דרשינן בתורת כהנים ובשחיטת קדשים (דף כח:) אם אינו ענין לחוץ לזמנו תנהו ענין לחוץ למקומו וליכא למימר דהאי כרת עליה קאי דכתיב בפגול גמור בצו את אהרן והנפש האוכלת ממנו עונה תשא ודרשינן בתורת כהנים ממנו עונה תשא ולא מחברו דהיינו חוץ למקומו דכתיב ביה מחשבה כותיה:
notes.en: Piggul is one of the fundamentals of the Torah: that one is liable to karet for it. And the verse did not teach it to be [punished] with karet; it is stated only in [the portion] Kedoshim Tihyu: “And whoever eats it shall bear his iniquity” [Leviticus 19:8]. And although piggul is written there, it is not speaking of full piggul but of one who intends during slaughter [to eat it] outside its place, for so we expound in Torat Kohanim and in [the chapter] Sheḥitat Kodashim (Zevaḥim 28b): if it is not relevant to [intent] outside its time, apply it to [intent] outside its place. And one cannot say that this karet applies to [intent outside its place], for concerning full piggul it is written in Tzav et Aharon: “And the soul that eats of it shall bear her iniquity” [Leviticus 7:18], and we expound in Torat Kohanim: “of it” shall bear her iniquity, and not of its fellow, that is, [intent] outside its place, of which an intention like it is written.

messages.text: Zavda bar Levi teaches: It is stated there, with regard to meat of an offering left over after the appointed time for its consumption [notar]: “But everyone who eats it shall bear his iniquity” (Leviticus 19:8), and it is stated here, with regard to intent to consume an offering after its appointed time: “And the soul that eats it shall bear his iniquity” (Leviticus 7:18). Just as there the punishment for eating notar is karet, so too here, the punishment for eating piggul is karet.
messages.lead: The Gemara explains that this is as

verse.he: וְאִם הֵאָכֹל יֵאָכֵל מִבְּשַׂר־זֶבַח שְׁלָמָיו בַּיּוֹם הַשְּׁלִישִׁי לֹא יֵרָצֶה הַמַּקְרִיב אֹתוֹ לֹא יֵחָשֵׁב לוֹ פִּגּוּל יִהְיֶה וְהַנֶּפֶשׁ הָאֹכֶלֶת מִמֶּנּוּ עֲוֺנָהּ תִּשָּׂא׃
verse.en: If any of the flesh of that sacrifice of well-being is eaten on the third day, it shall not be acceptable; it shall not count for the one who offered it. It is an offensive thing, and the person who eats of it shall bear the guilt.

notes.he: גבי נותר בפרשת קדושים תהיו ואוכליו עונו ישא וגו' מה (כאן) [להלן] בקדושים תהיו כרת דכתיב ונכרת:
notes.en: And it is stated there: concerning notar, in the portion Kedoshim Tihyu: “And whoever eats it shall bear his iniquity,” etc. Just as there, in Kedoshim Tihyu, it is karet, as it is written: “and [that soul] shall be cut off.”

notes.he: בצו את אהרן בפגול גמור והנפש האוכלת וגו' והתם כתיב לא יחשב דהיינו פגול גמור חוץ לזמנו:
notes.en: It is stated here: in Tzav et Aharon, concerning full piggul: “And the soul that eats,” etc.; and there it is written, “it shall not be credited,” which is full piggul, [intent] outside its time.

notes.he: שהרי פיגול במחשב לאוכלו חוץ לזמנו אחד מגופי תורה ולא למדו הכתוב לכרת אלא מג"ש דיליף עון עון מנותר נאמר כאן בנותר ואוכליו עונו ישא והאי פגול דהכא חוץ למקומו הוא דהא כתיב ביה הכא לא יחשב ונאמר להלן בפגול עונה תשא מה להלן בנותר כרת דכתיב ואוכליו וגו' ונכרתה וגו' אף כאן כרת:
notes.en: For piggul, one who intends to eat it outside its time, is one of the fundamentals of the Torah, and the verse taught it [to be punished] with karet only by a verbal analogy, for he derives “iniquity” and “iniquity” from notar. It is stated here, concerning notar: “And whoever eats it shall bear his iniquity”; and this piggul here is [intent] outside its place, for “it shall not be credited” is written of it here. And it is stated there concerning piggul: “shall bear her iniquity.” Just as there, concerning notar, it is karet, as it is written, “And whoever eats it,” etc., “and [that soul] shall be cut off,” etc., so too here it is karet.

messages.text: A verbal analogy should never be lightly regarded in your eyes, as the fact that one is punished with karet for consuming notar, from which it is derived that one is punished with karet for partaking of piggul, is one of the fundamental principles of the Torah, and the verse taught it only through a verbal analogy.

notes.he: לנותר בכרת אלא בגזירה שוה דלא ידעינן דהאי כרת דקדושים תהיו בנותר קמיירי דהא בתר דקרא דחוץ למקומו כתיב ומשמע דעליה קאי אלא משום דאתיא קדש קדש:
notes.en: And the verse taught it only: [the verse taught] notar [to be punished] with karet only through a verbal analogy, for we would not know that this karet of Kedoshim Tihyu speaks of notar, since it is written after the verse about [intent] outside its place and seems to refer to it; [we know it] only because of the verbal analogy “sacred” and “sacred.”

messages.text: What is this verbal analogy? One derives by verbal analogy of the word “sacred” in Leviticus and the word “sacred” in Exodus that the verse: “But everyone who eats it shall bear his iniquity,” is discussing notar. This verse states: “But everyone who eats it shall bear his iniquity, because he has profaned the sacred thing of the Lord” (Leviticus 19:8), and it is written: “You shall burn the leftovers [notar] in fire; they are not to be eaten, for they are sacred” (Exodus 29:34). Just as the verse in Exodus is referring to notar, the same is true of the verse in Leviticus.

verse.he: וְאִם־יִוָּתֵר מִבְּשַׂר הַמִּלֻּאִים וּמִן־הַלֶּחֶם עַד־הַבֹּקֶר וְשָׂרַפְתָּ אֶת־הַנּוֹתָר בָּאֵשׁ לֹא יֵאָכֵל כִּי־קֹדֶשׁ הוּא׃
verse.en: And if any of the flesh of ordination, or any of the bread, is left until morning, you shall put what is left to the fire; it shall not be eaten, for it is holy.

notes.he: לא למדו הכתוב אלא בג"ש דיליף קדש קדש כתיב הכא כי את קדש ה' חילל וכתיב התם ושרפת את הנותר באש לא יאכל כי קדש מה להלן נותר אף כאן נותר ולא פגול אע"ג דכתיב ביה פגול דחוץ למקומו הוא כמקומו:
notes.en: For notar: the verse taught it only by a verbal analogy, for he derives “sacred” and “sacred.” Here it is written: “because he has profaned the sacred thing of the Lord,” and there it is written: “You shall burn the leftovers in fire; it shall not be eaten, for it is sacred.” Just as there it is notar, so too here it is notar and not piggul, even though piggul is written in it, for that is [intent] outside its place, in keeping with its position [in the passage].

messages.text: A verbal analogy should never be lightly regarded in your eyes, as the fact that one is punished with karet for engaging in intercourse with one’s daughter born from the woman he raped is one of the fundamental principles of the Torah, and the verse taught it only through a verbal analogy.

notes.he: דבשריפה:
notes.en: One’s daughter from the woman he raped is one of the fundamentals of the Torah: that [the punishment] is by burning.

messages.text: Rabbi Yitzḥak bar Avdimi said to me that this halakha is derived by a verbal analogy between the unusual form “they [henna]” and “they [henna],” written with regard to the prohibition against engaging in intercourse with one’s daughter born from the woman he raped.

notes.he: כתיב באשתו (ויקרא י״ח:י״ז) ערות אשה ובתה לא תגלה דמשמע בתה ממנו ובתה מאחר סיפיה דקרא שארה הנה זמה היא וכתיב (שם) ערות בת בנך או בת בתך ובאנוסה כתיב דהא בת בתו מאשתו נפקא לו מקרא דלעיל ערות אשה ובתה ובתו לא כתיבא באנוסתו אלא אתיא הנה הנה מאשתו כתיב באשתו שארה הנה זמה היא וכתיב באנוסתו כי ערותך הנה מה התם כתיבא בתו דכתיב אשה ובתה אף כאן נמי באנוסה עשה בתו כבת בתו. וא"ת קל וחומר הוא אין מזהירין מן הדין:
notes.en: It is derived from “they” [henna] and “they”: it is written concerning one’s wife (Leviticus 18:17): “The nakedness of a woman and her daughter you shall not uncover,” which implies her daughter from him and her daughter from another man, and the end of that verse is: “they [henna] are near kinswomen; it is lewdness.” And it is written (ibid. [18:10]): “The nakedness of your son’s daughter or of your daughter’s daughter,” and that is written about a woman he raped, since his daughter’s daughter from his wife is already derived from the earlier verse, “the nakedness of a woman and her daughter.” And his daughter [herself] is not written concerning the woman he raped; rather, it is derived from “they” and “they” from his wife. Concerning his wife it is written, “they are near kinswomen; it is lewdness,” and concerning the woman he raped it is written, “for they are your own nakedness.” Just as there his daughter is written, as it is written, “a woman and her daughter,” so too here, concerning the woman he raped, [the verse] made his daughter like his daughter’s daughter. And if you say it is an a fortiori inference: one does not issue a prohibition on the basis of a logical inference.

notes.he: לא למדה אלא מג"ש דאמר ר' יצחק בר אבדימי אתיא הנה הנה לאיסורא כתיב הכא גבי לאו ערות אשה ובתה לא תגלה את בת בנה ואת בת בתה וגו' והאי דקאמר ערות אשה ובתה באשה שיש לו אישות בה קא מיירי לא שנא בתה שהיה לה מאחר לא שנא בתה שיש לה ממנו וכתיב ערות בת בנך או בת בתך לא תגלה ערותן כי ערותך הנה והכא לא כתיב אשה משמע דכל הני לאו באישות מיירי אלא באונס אשכחן בת בנו ובת בתו מאנוסתו בתו מאנוסתו מנין וכי תימא ק"ו אין עונשין מן הדין אלא אתיא הנה הנה לאיסורא מה כאן גבי ערות אשה ובתה גלי בבתו מאישות אף הכא בערות בת בנך או בת בתך מיחייב נמי אבתו מאנוסתו ואתיא זמה זמה לשרפה כתיב הכא גבי ערות אשה ובתה זמה וכבר ילפינן בתו מאנוסתו נמי מיניה דכתיב ביה נמי (הנה שארה הנה זמה היא) וכתב בשרפה זמה דכתב ואיש אשר יקח את אשה ואת אמה זמה היא מה זו בשרפה אף זו בשרפה ובתו מאנוסתו נמי:
notes.en: For one’s daughter from the woman he raped: [the verse] taught it only by a verbal analogy, as Rabbi Yitzḥak bar Avdimi said: it is derived from “they” and “they” for the prohibition. It is written here, concerning the prohibition: “The nakedness of a woman and her daughter you shall not uncover; you shall not take her son’s daughter or her daughter’s daughter,” etc. And this that it says, “the nakedness of a woman and her daughter,” speaks of a woman with whom he has marriage, whether her daughter whom she had from another man or her daughter whom she has from him. And it is written: “The nakedness of your son’s daughter or of your daughter’s daughter, you shall not uncover their nakedness, for they are your own nakedness”; and here “woman” is not written, which implies that all these do not speak of marriage but of rape. We have found his son’s daughter and his daughter’s daughter from the woman he raped; from where do we know his daughter from the woman he raped? And if you say an a fortiori inference: one does not punish on the basis of a logical inference. Rather, it is derived from “they” and “they” for the prohibition: just as here, concerning “the nakedness of a woman and her daughter,” [the verse] revealed [the law of] his daughter from marriage, so too here, concerning “the nakedness of your son’s daughter or your daughter’s daughter,” he is also liable for his daughter from the woman he raped. And it is derived from “lewdness” and “lewdness” for burning: it is written here, concerning “the nakedness of a woman and her daughter,” “lewdness,” and we have already derived his daughter from the woman he raped from it as well, since it is written of it too [Editor’s note: it appears it should read: since “for they are your own nakedness” is also written of it, and we derive “they” and “they” from there, so it is as though “lewdness” were also written of it; and it is written regarding burning, etc.] (“they are near kinswomen; it is lewdness”). And it is written regarding burning, “lewdness,” as it is written: “And if a man takes a woman and her mother, it is lewdness.” Just as this is by burning, so too this is by burning, and his daughter from the woman he raped as well.

messages.text: As it is written: “The nakedness of a woman and her daughter…you shall not take her son’s daughter, or her daughter’s daughter, to uncover her nakedness: They [henna] are near kinswomen” (Leviticus 18:17). And it is stated: “The nakedness of your son’s daughter, or of your daughter’s daughter; for they [henna] are your own nakedness” (Leviticus 18:10). This latter verse is interpreted as referring to one’s granddaughter from the woman he raped (see Yevamot 97a).

verse.he: עֶרְוַת אִשָּׁה וּבִתָּהּ לֹא תְגַלֵּה אֶת־בַּת־בְּנָהּ וְאֶת־בַּת־בִּתָּהּ לֹא תִקַּח לְגַלּוֹת עֶרְוָתָהּ שַׁאֲרָה הֵנָּה זִמָּה הִוא׃
verse.en: Do not uncover the nakedness of a woman and her daughter; nor shall you take to wife her son’s daughter or her daughter’s daughter and uncover her nakedness: they are kindred; it is depravity.

messages.text: The verbal analogy teaches that although one’s daughter from the woman he raped is not mentioned in the verse, she too is included with one’s granddaughter, just as a daughter and a granddaughter are equated in Leviticus 18:17.

Furthermore, the punishment for this transgression of intercourse with one’s daughter from the woman he raped is derived from a verbal analogy between: “It is lewdness” (Leviticus 18:17), which is written with regard to engaging in intercourse with both a woman and her daughter, and the same term “lewdness” that appears elsewhere, which teaches that the transgressor is liable to be put to death by burning.

notes.he: כי יקח איש את אשה ואת אמה זמה היא (ויקרא כ׳:י״ד):
notes.en: “Lewdness” and “lewdness” for burning: “If a man takes a woman and her mother, it is lewdness” (Leviticus 20:14).

messages.text: As it is stated: “And if a man take with his wife also her mother, it is lewdness; they shall be burnt with fire, both he and they” (Leviticus 20:14). This teaches that death by burning is the punishment for engaging in intercourse with both a woman and her daughter, and the same applies to intercourse with one’s daughter from the woman he raped, due to the verbal analogy of henna and henna linking the two cases.

verse.he: וְאִישׁ אֲשֶׁר יִקַּח אֶת־אִשָּׁה וְאֶת־אִמָּהּ זִמָּה הִוא בָּאֵשׁ יִשְׂרְפוּ אֹתוֹ וְאֶתְהֶן וְלֹא־תִהְיֶה זִמָּה בְּתוֹכְכֶם׃
verse.en: If a man marries a woman and her mother, it is depravity; both he and they shall be put to the fire, that there be no depravity among you.

messages.text: A verbal analogy should not be lightly regarded in your eyes, as the list of those who are liable to be put to death by stoning is one of the fundamental principles of the Torah, and the verse taught it only through a verbal analogy.

notes.he: רוב חייבי סקילה כגון הבא על האם ועל הכלה לא כתיבא סקילה אלא דמיהם בם (שם):
notes.en: Those who are stoned: for most of those liable to stoning, such as one who has intercourse with his mother or with his daughter-in-law, stoning is not written, only “their blood shall be upon them” (ibid. [Leviticus 20]).

messages.text: It is stated here, with regard to engaging in intercourse with specific relatives: “Their blood shall be upon them” (Leviticus 20:11–16), and it is stated with regard to a necromancer and a sorcerer: “Their blood shall be upon them” (Leviticus 20:27). Just as there, the verse specifies that a necromancer and a sorcerer are executed by stoning, so too here, with regard to one who engages in intercourse with those relatives, they are executed by stoning.
messages.lead: This is as it is taught in a baraita:

verse.he: וְאִישׁ אוֹ־אִשָּׁה כִּי־יִהְיֶה בָהֶם אוֹב אוֹ יִדְּעֹנִי מוֹת יוּמָתוּ בָּאֶבֶן יִרְגְּמוּ אֹתָם דְּמֵיהֶם בָּם׃ {פ}
verse.en: A man or a woman who has a ghost or a familiar spirit shall be put to death; they shall be pelted with stones—and the bloodguilt is theirs.

notes.he: מה אוב וידעוני בסקילה דכתיב באבן ירגמו אותם דמיהם בם:
notes.en: Just as a necromancer and a sorcerer are by stoning, as it is written: “They shall stone them with stones; their blood shall be upon them.”

messages.text: § The mishna’s list of prohibitions for whose unwitting violation one must bring a sin offering includes one who blends the anointing oil according to the specifications of the oil prepared by Moses in the wilderness (see Exodus 30:22–33). The Sages taught in a baraita:

One who blends the anointing oil to learn how it was prepared or to transfer it to the community for them to use in the Temple is exempt. But if he blends the anointing oil in order to apply it to his body he is liable.

notes.he: לסוך ממנו חייב דכתיב (שמות ל׳:ל״ג) אשר ירקח כמוהו:
notes.en: One who blends: to apply from it, is liable, as it is written (Exodus 30:33): “Whoever compounds any like it.”

notes.he: ע"מ לסוך ממנו חייב ואינו מוסר לציבור ועובר משום על בשר אדם לא ייסך ובמתכונתו וכו' ואחד הסך ממנו שלא עשה פטור אע"פ שמסרה זה לציבור מ"ט לפי שאין חייבין כו':
notes.en: One who blends: in order to apply from it, is liable; [that is, he] does not hand it over to the community, and he transgresses “Upon the flesh of a person it shall not be poured” and “according to its composition,” etc. And likewise one who applies from it, who did not make it, is exempt, even though the other handed it over to the community. What is the reason? Because one is liable only, etc.

messages.text: And one who applies to his body the oil prepared by another is exempt, because he is liable for applying the oil to his body only if he uses the anointing oil that was prepared by Moses alone, in accordance with the verse: “Or whoever puts any of it upon a stranger” (Exodus 30:33), which is referring to that specific oil.

verse.he: אִישׁ אֲשֶׁר יִרְקַח כָּמֹהוּ וַאֲשֶׁר יִתֵּן מִמֶּנּוּ עַל־זָר וְנִכְרַת מֵעַמָּיו׃ {ס}
verse.en: Anyone who compounds its like, or puts any of it on a lay person, shall be cut off from kin.

notes.he: אחר שלא פטמו:
notes.en: And one who applies from it: when he did not blend it [himself].

notes.he: ואשר יתן ממנו מאותו של משה:
notes.en: “Or whoever puts any of it”: of that [oil] of Moses.

messages.text: One who blends the anointing oil to learn how it was prepared or in order to transfer it to the community for them to use in the Temple is exempt. From where do we derive this?
messages.quote: to learn how it was prepared or to transfer it to the community … is exempt

messages.text: This is derived via a verbal analogy from the term: “Its composition” (Exodus 30:32), written with regard to the oil and the term: “According to its composition” (Exodus 30:37), written with regard to the incense. And it is written with regard to the incense in that verse: “You shall not prepare for yourselves,” from which it is inferred that it is incense prepared for yourselves that is prohibited, but if one prepares it to transfer it to the community he is exempt. With regard to the anointing oil as well, one who blends it to transfer it to the community is exempt.

verse.he: וְהַקְּטֹרֶת אֲשֶׁר תַּעֲשֶׂה בְּמַתְכֻּנְתָּהּ לֹא תַעֲשׂוּ לָכֶם קֹדֶשׁ תִּהְיֶה לְךָ לַיהֹוָה׃
verse.en: But when you make this incense, you must not make any in the same proportions for yourselves; it shall be held by you sacred to GOD.

messages.text: The Gemara objects: But in light of this verbal analogy, let the case of incense return and let us derive it from that of the anointing oil: Just as with regard to the anointing oil, when one blends it in halves, i.e., not all the specified amount at once, he is exempt, so too, with regard to the incense, when one blends it in halves he should be exempt.

notes.he: כגון ו' לוגין דההוא דמשה הוה הין י"ב לוגין:
notes.en: In halves: for example, six log, since that of Moses was a hin, twelve log.

notes.he: ליה לחצאין פטור כדמפרש לקמיה:
notes.en: Just as with the oil, when he blends it in halves he is exempt, as is explained further on.

messages.text: Why, then, does Rava say: In the case of incense that one blended in halves, he is liable, whereas with regard to anointing oil that one blended in halves, he is exempt?

notes.he: חצאין דקטרת קפ"ד מנין דבכל יום היה מקטיר מנה כדאמרינן לקמן (כריתות ד' ו.) שס"ה מנין (כמנין ימות החמה):
notes.en: Halves of the incense: 184 maneh, since every day he burned a maneh, as we say below (Keritot 6a): 365 maneh, corresponding to the number of days of the solar year.

messages.text: Rava could say to you: With regard to the anointing oil it is written: “Neither shall you prepare any like it according to its composition” (Exodus 30:32), which indicates that it is oil prepared precisely like it that is prohibited, but with regard to preparing half of it, one may well do so.

verse.he: עַל־בְּשַׂר אָדָם לֹא יִיסָךְ וּבְמַתְכֻּנְתּוֹ לֹא תַעֲשׂוּ כָּמֹהוּ קֹדֶשׁ הוּא קֹדֶשׁ יִהְיֶה לָכֶם׃
verse.en: It must not be rubbed on any person’s body, and you must not make anything like it in the same proportions; it is sacred, to be held sacred by you.

messages.text: By contrast, with regard to incense, as it is written: “And the incense that you shall prepare, according to its composition you shall not prepare for yourselves” (Exodus 30:37), which teaches that any act of preparing of this incense is prohibited, as it is possible to burn a portion, half of the maneh that must be prepared, in the morning, and a portion in the afternoon.

notes.he: חצי מנה:
notes.en: A portion [peras] in the morning: half a maneh.

notes.he: כתיב כל עשייה דקטרת כלומר כל אותו שיעור שמקטיר אסור לפטם כמוהו ואפשר דמקטר קטרת לחצאין פרס שחרית ופרס בין הערבים דמנה היה מקטיר בכל יום משום הכי כי מפטים לחצאין חייב:
notes.en: “That you shall make”: is written [meaning] every making of incense; that is, that whole measure that is burned, it is forbidden to blend like it. And it is possible to burn the incense in halves, a portion in the morning and a portion in the afternoon, since one maneh was burned each day. Therefore, when he blends it in halves he is liable.

messages.text: The anointing oil contains pure myrrh weighing 500 shekels, cassia of 500 shekels, aromatic cinnamon of 500 shekels, and aromatic calamus of 250 shekels. It is found that all of them together amount to 1,750 shekels.

notes.he: שקלים:
notes.en: Five hundred: shekels.

notes.he: דהכי אמר קרא מחציתו חמשים ומאתים דלהכי נקט מחציתו שלא יהו שוקלים אותו הכל ביחד אלא לחצאין כדי שיהו שם שתי הכרעות:
notes.en: Aromatic cinnamon, five hundred: for so the verse says: “half of it, two hundred and fifty.” It said “half of it” for this reason: that they should not weigh it all together but in halves, so that there would be two surpluses there.

messages.text: Does the tanna come to teach us the tally? Why is it necessary for the baraita to state the sum of the amounts?
messages.quote: all of them together amount to 1,750 shekels

messages.text: This is difficult for the tanna: Since the verse states: “And of aromatic cinnamon half so much, two hundred and fifty, and of aromatic calamus two hundred and fifty” (Exodus 30:23), one might say that the weight of aromatic calamus is like that of aromatic cinnamon: Just as half of the amount of aromatic cinnamon is two hundred and fifty, so too, the verse means that half of the amount of aromatic calamus is two hundred and fifty, which would mean that the sum total is two thousand.

verse.he: וְאַתָּה קַח־לְךָ בְּשָׂמִים רֹאשׁ מׇר־דְּרוֹר חֲמֵשׁ מֵאוֹת וְקִנְּמׇן־בֶּשֶׂם מַחֲצִיתוֹ חֲמִשִּׁים וּמָאתָיִם וּקְנֵה־בֹשֶׂם חֲמִשִּׁים וּמָאתָיִם׃
verse.en: Next take choice spices: five hundred weight of solidified myrrh, half as much—two hundred and fifty—of fragrant cinnamon, two hundred and fifty of aromatic cane,

notes.he: כלומר להכי אשמעינן ברייתא דאי ממשמעותא דקרא הוה אמינא קנה בושם כקנמן בשם דמחציתו דקרא אתרוייהו קאי קמ"ל:
notes.en: This is what was difficult for the tanna: that is, this is why the baraita teaches us [the total], for from the plain sense of the verse I would have said that aromatic calamus is like aromatic cinnamon, that the verse’s “half of it” refers to both of them. [The baraita] teaches us [otherwise].

notes.dh: אף קנה בשם מחציתו חמשים ומאתים
notes.he: כלומר דכולה חמש מאות והוו להו תרי אלפין:
notes.en: Also aromatic calamus, half of it two hundred and fifty: that is, that all of it is five hundred, and they would come to two thousand.

messages.text: But why not say that it is indeed so, that the total weight of calamus is five hundred?

notes.he: נימא תרין אלפין:
notes.en: But say that it is indeed so: let us say two thousand.

messages.text: If so, let the verse write: And of aromatic cinnamon and of aromatic calamus half so much and half so much, two hundred and fifty. The fact that the verse employs the term “half so much” only with regard to cinnamon indicates that their weights were different.

notes.he: שהיו שוקלין לחצאין:
notes.en: Half and half: that they would weigh in halves.

notes.dh: א"כ נימא קרא לתרווייהו לקינמון בשם ולקנה בשם מחציתו חמשים ומאתים
notes.he: מדלא קאמר לקנה בשם מחציתו ש"מ דאלף ותש"נ:
notes.en: If so, let the verse say for both, for aromatic cinnamon and for aromatic calamus: half of it, two hundred and fifty. Since it does not say “half of it” for calamus, conclude from it that it is one thousand seven hundred and fifty.

messages.text: @Abaye When one weighs these substances, does he weigh the ingredients with a slight surplus, so that they tip the scales, or does he weigh the ingredients with precision?

notes.he: שאין הבשם מכריע:
notes.en: Precisely [ayin be’ayin]: so that the spice does not tip [the scale].

messages.text: The Merciful One writes: “Of each there shall be a like weight” (Exodus 30:34), which indicates a precise measure, and you say it is possible that one weighs the ingredients with a surplus?

verse.he: וַיֹּאמֶר יְהֹוָה אֶל־מֹשֶׁה קַח־לְךָ סַמִּים נָטָף ׀ וּשְׁחֵלֶת וְחֶלְבְּנָה סַמִּים וּלְבֹנָה זַכָּה בַּד בְּבַד יִהְיֶה׃
verse.en: And GOD said to Moses: Take the herbs stacte, onycha, and galbanum—these herbs together with pure frankincense; let there be an equal part of each.

notes.he: מתקל במתקל דהיינו עין בעין:
notes.en: The Merciful One writes “a like weight” [bad bevad]: weight against weight, that is, precisely.

notes.he: כלומר שהיה שוקל ההכרעות אח"כ לבד לידע כמה הכרע יש בהן אלא מדכתיב בד בבד אלמא לית בהן הכרע:
notes.en: And you say with a surplus: that is, that he would afterward weigh the surpluses by themselves to know how much surplus there is in them. But since it is written “a like weight,” evidently there is no surplus in them.

messages.text: The Gemara raises a difficulty: But doesn’t Rabbi Yehuda say: The Holy One, Blessed be He, knows the amount of surpluses that should be added. Evidently, there is a surplus involved in these measures.

notes.he: שלא היה שוקל ההכרעות לבד אלא מניחן כמות שהן והמקום יודע מה משקלו. פירוש רומי:
notes.en: [The printed text marks this comment “ע״א”.] The Omnipresent knows the surpluses: that he would not weigh the surpluses by themselves, but leaves them as they are, and the Omnipresent knows what their weight is. [The comment ends with the words “perush Romi.”]

notes.dh: והאמר רב יהודה המקום הוא יודע בהכרעות
notes.he: כלומר שלא היה שוקל ההכרעות לבד אלא מניחן כמות שהן והמקום יודע מה משקלן אלמא דאית ליה הכרע לכל שקל:
notes.en: But doesn’t Rav Yehuda say: The Omnipresent knows the surpluses [Rabbeinu Gershom, like the Aramaic of the daf, reads Rav Yehuda; the English translation has Rabbi Yehuda]: that is, he would not weigh the surpluses by themselves, but leaves them as they are, and the Omnipresent knows what their weight is. Evidently he holds that there is a surplus for every shekel.

messages.text: The Aramaic here reads Rav Yehuda, as in the next line; the English translation has Rabbi Yehuda.

With regard to aromatic cinnamon, why does one bring half of its total of five hundred, i.e., two hundred and fifty at one time, and two hundred and fifty at one time? Since its entire amount is five hundred, let him bring five hundred all at once.
messages.lead: Rather, one certainly weighs with a surplus, and this is what

notes.he: אלא אמר רב יהודה הכי קשיא ליה כו' - ה"ג אלא אמר רב יהודה - מדקא מייתי ליה תרי זימני ודאי לאפושי הוא דעבד:
notes.en: Rather, Rav Yehuda said, this is what was difficult for him, etc. [Rashi’s heading includes “this is what was difficult for him,” which the printed Gemara does not have.] This is the reading: “Rather, Rav Yehuda said.” Since he brings it twice, he certainly does so in order to add [a surplus].

notes.he: אמר לך אביי רב יהודה דאית ליה הכרע יליף מהכא דסבר קנמון בשם אמאי מייתו במחציות בתרין זמני אלא ש"מ למילף דאית בהו הכרע והמקום יודע כמה הכרעות ואין שעור להכרע:
notes.en: Abaye could say to you [in Rabbeinu Gershom’s version this answer is Abaye’s]: Rav Yehuda, who holds there is a surplus, derives it from here, for he holds: aromatic cinnamon, why do they bring it in halves, in two times? Rather, conclude from it that there is a surplus in them, and the Omnipresent knows how many surpluses, and there is no fixed measure for the surplus.

messages.text: Conclude from the fact that one brings aromatic cinnamon at two separate times that there is a surplus involved in this measure, i.e., one must add a little each time he weighs the cinnamon, and the Holy One, Blessed be He, knows the amount of surpluses.

notes.he: לישנא אחרינא מכלל דאית ביה הכרע דאמר ר' יהודה קנמון בשם אמאי מייתי מחציתו חמש מאות ומאתים כו':
notes.en: Another version: from which it follows that there is a surplus in it, as R. Yehuda said: aromatic cinnamon, why do they bring half of it, of five hundred, two hundred [and fifty], etc. [Editor’s note: that is, the other version does not read “Rather, Rav Yehuda could say to you,” but only “as Rav Yehuda said,” etc., and Rav Yehuda himself brought proof from the verse. It appears that this is why Rashi wrote “this is the reading: Rather, Rav Yehuda said,” etc., meaning to exclude the reading of the other version.]

messages.text: But according to Rav Yehuda’s opinion, what is the meaning of the phrase: “Of each there shall be a like weight”?

It means that one should not place a weight of one ingredient against the weight of another ingredient and weigh in this manner. In other words, after weighing one of the ingredients one may not weigh another ingredient against that one; rather, each ingredient must be weighed independently against the scales.

notes.he: שישקול כל בשם ובשם כנגד הברזל ולא ישקול במניין דמר דרור ויחזור וישקול קדה כנגד מר דרור:
notes.en: That one should not place a weight, etc.: that he should weigh each and every spice against the iron [weight], and not weigh by the count of the myrrh and then go back and weigh the cassia against the myrrh.

notes.he: דקאמר לא דמשמע עין בעין אלא שלא יניח משקל במשקל ויתקול. כלומר שלא יניח משקל האבן של חמשים ומאתים עם החמשים ומאתים וישקול שקל של חמש מאות כן אלא לכל משקל יניח אבנו היינו בד בבד:
notes.en: And what is “a like weight” that it says? Not that it means precisely, but that one should not place a weight [together with] a weight and weigh. That is, he should not place the stone weight of two hundred and fifty with the [other] two hundred and fifty and weigh a shekel-weight of five hundred that way; rather, for each weight he should place its own stone. That is “a like weight.”

messages.text: How did they prepare the anointing oil that Moses prepared in the wilderness? They would cook the roots of the spices in it; this is the statement of Rabbi Yehuda.

notes.he: בבשמים:
notes.en: The roots: of the spices.

notes.he: דכתיב ושמן זית הין בו שלקו (את) [עם] העיקרין מר דרור כו' כדי שיקלטו ריח:
notes.en: The anointing oil that Moses made in the wilderness: as it is written, “And of olive oil a hin” [Exodus 30:24]; in it they cooked the roots, the myrrh, etc., so that they would absorb the fragrance.

messages.text: @Rabbi Yehuda But that amount of oil is not sufficient even to apply to the roots, as they would absorb the oil; how, then, could the roots be cooked in it?

notes.he: דשמן לא הוה אלא י"ב לוגין ועיקרין הוו טובא:
notes.en: Is not sufficient: since the oil was only twelve log, and the roots were many.

messages.text: Instead, how did they act? They brought the roots and boiled them in water and the fragrant substance would rise to the top, and one poured the anointing oil on the water, and the oil would absorb the fragrance and retain it, and later he removed the oil [vekipeḥo] from off the top and place it in its flask. This is how the anointing oil was prepared.

notes.he: שיבלעו המים ולכשיציף עליהן השמן לא יבלעוהו:
notes.en: And soaked them in water [Rashi reads “soaked”; the printed text reads “boiled”]: so that they would absorb the water, and when he floated the oil over them they would not absorb it.

notes.he: קנחו וחברו קפחת את הרועה ביומא (דף פג:) קנחו משה לשמן מעל העיקרין ונתנו בצלוחית:
notes.en: And the oil absorbed the fragrance, and he removed it [vekipeḥo]: he wiped it off; its like is “kipaḥta et haro’eh” in Yoma (83b). Moses wiped the oil off the roots and put it in a flask.

notes.he: אלא הביא עיקר ושראום במים כדי שלא יבלעו מן השמן והיה זורק המים לחוץ והיה זורק השמן על גבי העיקרין והציף עליהן שמן שיהו מכוסין וקלט השמן את הריח מן הבשמים:
notes.en: Rather, he brought the roots and they soaked them in water so that they would not absorb any of the oil. And he would throw the water out and pour the oil over the roots, and he floated oil over them so that they would be covered, and the oil absorbed the fragrance from the spices.

notes.he: והיה מסירו מיד כדי שלא יבלעו העיקרין השמן:
notes.en: And removed it [vekipeḥo]: he would remove it at once, so that the roots would not absorb the oil.

messages.text: @Rabbi Yosei …

notes.he: מה צורך בכך וכי נס אחד כו':
notes.en: Rabbi Yehuda said to him: What need is there for this? And was just one miracle, etc. [An editor’s note here marks the end of the material that belongs to 5a.]

messages.text: 5b
And was just one miracle performed with the anointing oil? But many miracles were performed with it, from its initial preparation to its end.

notes.he: שאתה מתמיה שאינו ספק אפילו לסוך אהרן ובניו כל ז' ימי המלואים כדמפרש בפ"ק דיומא (דף ה.) שבעת ימים ימלא את ידכם (ויקרא ח׳:ל״ג) ואיתקש משיחה לריבוי דכתיב למשחה בהם ולמלא בם את ידם (שמות כ״ט:כ״ט):
notes.en: And was just one miracle performed with it: [as if to say,] you wonder that it would not suffice? [It sufficed] even to anoint Aaron and his sons all seven days of inauguration, as is explained in the first chapter of Yoma (5a): “Seven days shall he consecrate you” (Leviticus 8:33), and anointing is juxtaposed to consecration, as it is written: “to be anointed in them and to be consecrated in them” (Exodus 29:29).

messages.text: Its initial preparation was only the measure of twelve log, and even so the Tabernacle and its vessels were anointed with it, and likewise Aaron and his sons were anointed with it all the seven days of inauguration, and High Priests and kings were anointed with it throughout the generations, and yet despite the reduction in the amount of oil during its preparation process, as well as its multiple uses throughout history, it all remains intact for its use in the future.

As it is stated: “This [zeh] shall be a sacred anointing oil to Me throughout your generations” (Exodus 30:31). The word zeh has a numerical value [bigimatriya] of twelve, which teaches that the original twelve log of oil that existed at the outset are extant throughout all the generations. If so, i.e., if such miracles were performed in connection with the oil, it is no wonder that its initial preparation was miraculous.

verse.he: וְאֶל־בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל תְּדַבֵּר לֵאמֹר שֶׁמֶן מִשְׁחַת־קֹדֶשׁ יִהְיֶה זֶה לִי לְדֹרֹתֵיכֶם׃
verse.en: And speak to the Israelite people, as follows: This shall be an anointing oil sacred to Me throughout the ages.

notes.he: אלמא כולהו י"ב לוגין דקיימי לעתיד לבוא:
notes.en: “This shall be to Me throughout your generations”: evidently all twelve log remain for the future.

messages.text: “And Moses took the anointing oil, and anointed the Tabernacle and all that was in it and sanctified them” (Leviticus 8:10).

verse.he: וַיִּקַּח מֹשֶׁה אֶת־שֶׁמֶן הַמִּשְׁחָה וַיִּמְשַׁח אֶת־הַמִּשְׁכָּן וְאֶת־כׇּל־אֲשֶׁר־בּוֹ וַיְקַדֵּשׁ אֹתָם׃
verse.en: Moses took the anointing oil and anointed the Tabernacle and all that was in it, thus consecrating them.

messages.text: With regard to the anointing oil that Moses prepared in the wilderness, many miracles were performed with it, from its initial preparation to its end. Its initial preparation was only twelve log; consider how much of it a cauldron absorbs from what is cooked inside it, and how much of it the roots of the plants absorb, how much of it the fire burns, and yet the Tabernacle, and its vessels, and Aaron, and his sons were all anointed with it all seven days of the inauguration.
And High Priests and kings were anointed with it,
and even a High Priest, the son of a High Priest, requires anointing with the oil.
But one does not anoint a king, the son of a king.

And if you say: If so, for what reason did they anoint King Solomon, who was the son of King David? It was due to the dispute over the throne instigated by his older brother Adonijah, who attempted to usurp the monarchy. And similarly Joash, son of Ahaziah, was anointed king (see II Kings 11:12) due to the threat of Athaliah, his paternal grandmother, who attempted to seize the monarchy for herself (II Kings 11:1–3).

And Jehoahaz, son of Josiah, was anointed as king (II Kings 23:30) due to the competition from Jehoiakim, his brother, who was two years older than his brother, i.e., Jehoahaz. Ordinarily the older brother succeeds the father, but Jehoahaz was more worthy of the throne.

notes.he: היה גדול מיהואחז ב' שנים דכתיב בו (מלכים ב כ״ג:ל״א) יהואחז בן עשרים ושלש שנה היה במלכו וג' חדשים מלך וביהויקים כתיב (שם) בן עשרים וחמש שנה היה במלכו נמצא יהויקים גדול מיהואחז ב' שנים כך שנויה בסדר עולם:
notes.en: Jehoiakim: was older than Jehoahaz by two years, as it is written of [Jehoahaz] (II Kings 23:31): “Jehoahaz was twenty-three years old when he became king, and he reigned three months,” and of Jehoiakim it is written (ibid. [23:36]): “He was twenty-five years old when he became king.” So Jehoiakim is found to be older than Jehoahaz by two years. So it is taught in Seder Olam.

messages.text: And even a High Priest, the son of a High Priest, requires anointing. From where do we derive this halakha?
messages.lead: The Gemara clarifies several aspects of this baraita. The Master said earlier:
messages.quote: even a High Priest, the son of a High Priest, requires anointing

messages.text: It is derived from a verse, as it is written: “And the anointed priest that shall be in his stead from among his sons” (Leviticus 6:15). Let the verse say merely: The priest that shall be in his stead from among his sons. What is taught by the addition of the term “anointed”? This teaches us that even when the new High Priest is from among the sons of the previous High Priest, only that priest who is anointed with oil is the High Priest, but if he is not anointed with oil he is not the High Priest.

verse.he: וְהַכֹּהֵן הַמָּשִׁיחַ תַּחְתָּיו מִבָּנָיו יַעֲשֶׂה אֹתָהּ חׇק־עוֹלָם לַיהֹוָה כָּלִיל תׇּקְטָר׃
verse.en: And so shall the priest, anointed from among his sons to succeed him, prepare it; it is GOD’s—a law for all time—to be turned entirely into smoke.

messages.text: But one does not anoint a king, the son of a king. From where do we derive this halakha?
messages.quote: But one does not anoint a king, the son of a king

messages.text: This is as it is written: In order that he may prolong his days in his kingdom, he and his sons, all the days in the midst of Israel (see Deuteronomy 17:20). The mention of a king’s sons teaches that the kingdom is an inheritance, which does not need to be confirmed by anointing.

verse.he: לְבִלְתִּי רוּם־לְבָבוֹ מֵאֶחָיו וּלְבִלְתִּי סוּר מִן־הַמִּצְוָה יָמִין וּשְׂמֹאול לְמַעַן יַאֲרִיךְ יָמִים עַל־מַמְלַכְתּוֹ הוּא וּבָנָיו בְּקֶרֶב יִשְׂרָאֵל׃ {ס}
verse.en: Thus he will not act haughtily toward his fellows or deviate from the Instruction to the right or to the left, to the end that he and his descendants may reign long in the midst of Israel.

notes.he: מלכות ירושה היא ואין צריך משיחה:
notes.en: The kingdom is an inheritance, and it does not require anointing.

messages.text: And for what reason did they anoint King Solomon? Due to the dispute over the throne instigated by his older brother Adonijah. From where do we derive that in a situation where there is a dispute the new king requires anointing, and the current king cannot simply grant the kingship as an inheritance to whomever he desires?
messages.quote: for what reason did they anoint King Solomon … due to the dispute

notes.dh: ולאו כל אימת דבעי מלך מורית
notes.he: מלכות לבניו בלא משיחה:
notes.en: And not whenever the king wishes does he bequeath the kingdom to his sons without anointing.

messages.text: The verse states: “He and his children in the midst of Israel” (Deuteronomy 17:20). At a time when there is peace in Israel the monarchy transfers smoothly to the king’s son, but not when there is a dispute.

notes.he: הוי המלכות ירושה ולא בעי משיחה אבל כי איכא מחלוקת לאו ירושה היא ובעי משיחה בתחלה:
notes.en: At a time when there is peace in Israel: the kingdom is an inheritance and does not require anointing; but when there is a dispute, it is not an inheritance, and it requires anointing at the outset.

notes.he: בזמן ששוכן בקרב ישראל בשלום דאין מחלוקת בינייהו מוריש מלכות לבניו:
notes.en: “In the midst of Israel”: at a time when he dwells in the midst of Israel in peace, when there is no dispute among them, he bequeaths the kingdom to his sons.

messages.text: Also Jehu, son of Jehoshaphat, son of Nimshi, was anointed by Elisha the prophet only due to the dispute with Joram, son of Ahab, who was the incumbent king, against whose reign Jehu rebelled (see II Kings 9:1–6).

Why is it necessary to state this reason? Let the tanna of the baraita derive that Jehu required anointing due to the fact that he was the first king of his lineage, as Jehu was not the son of a king.
messages.quote: Jehu, son of Nimshi, was anointed only due to the dispute

notes.he: דלא היה בן מלך:
notes.en: Let him derive it from the fact that he was the first king: since he was not the son of a king.

messages.text: The baraita is incomplete, and this is what it is teaching: One anoints the kings of the house of David with the anointing oil, but one does not anoint the kings from the kingdom of Israel. And if you say: For what reason did Elisha anoint Jehu, son of Jehoshaphat, son of Nimshi? This was due to the dispute with Joram, son of Ahab.

notes.he: משבא דוד אבל שאול נמשח:
notes.en: But not the kings of Israel: from when David came; but Saul was anointed.

notes.he: מדוד ואילך דכתיב ביה מיעוט זה טעון משיחה ולא אחר אבל שאול דהוי קודם לכן נמשח:
notes.en: The kings of Israel are not anointed: from David onward, since concerning him a limitation is written: “this one” requires anointing and not another. But Saul, who was before that, was anointed.

messages.text: One anoints the kings of the house of David with the anointing oil, but one does not anoint the kings of Israel. From where do we derive this halakha?
messages.quote: One anoints the kings of the house of David, but one does not anoint the kings of Israel

messages.text: It is derived from a verse, as it is written with regard to the anointing of David: “Arise, anoint him; for this is he” (I Samuel 16:12). This king, i.e., any king from the house of David, requires anointing, but another king, i.e., from the kingdom of Israel, whose kings were not descendants of the house of David, does not require anointing.

verse.he:
וַיִּשְׁלַח וַיְבִיאֵהוּ וְהוּא אַדְמוֹנִי עִם־יְפֵה עֵינַיִם וְטוֹב רֹאִי {פ}
וַיֹּאמֶר יְהֹוָה קוּם מְשָׁחֵהוּ כִּי־זֶה הוּא׃
verse.en: So they sent and brought him. He was ruddy-cheeked, bright-eyed, and handsome. And GOD said, “Rise and anoint him, for this is the one.”

messages.text: due to the dispute with Joram. And due to the dispute with Joram, son of Ahab, will we misuse consecrated property by anointing someone unnecessarily with the anointing oil, which is called “a sacred anointing oil” (Exodus 30:31)? After all, kings of the kingdom of Israel do not require anointing.
messages.lead: The Master said earlier that Jehu was anointed
messages.quote: due to the dispute with Joram

notes.dh: ומפני מחלוקתו של יורם נמשח כו'
notes.he: דבשלמא מלך בן מלך דבית דוד כי איכא מחלוקת נפקא לן מקראי דהדר למילתיה קמייתא למשיחה אבל מלכי ישראל לא חזו למשיחה כלל:
notes.en: And due to the dispute with Joram he was anointed, etc.: granted, a king son of a king of the house of David: when there is a dispute, we derive from the verses that he returns to the original rule of anointing. But the kings of Israel are not fit for anointing at all.

messages.text: This is as Rav Pappa said with regard to Jehoahaz: They anointed him with pure balsam oil, rather than with the anointing oil. Here too, Elisha anointed Jehu with pure balsam oil, not the anointing oil.

notes.he: נמשח ולא בשמן המשחה:
notes.en: With pure balsam: he was anointed, and not with the anointing oil.

notes.he: כדאמר רב פפא לקמן באפרסמא דכיא משחוהו שהיה יהויקים גדול ממנו ב' שנים:
notes.en: As Rav Pappa says below: they anointed him with pure balsam, since Jehoiakim was older than him by two years.

messages.text: And Jehoahaz, son of Josiah, was anointed due to the competition from Jehoiakim, his brother, who was two years older than him. And was Jehoiakim in fact older than Jehoahaz?
messages.lead: It was further stated in the baraita:
messages.quote: Jehoahaz … due to the competition from Jehoiakim, his brother, who was two years older

messages.text: But isn’t it written: “And the sons of Josiah: The firstborn Johanan, the second Jehoiakim, the third Zedekiah, the fourth Shallum” (I Chronicles 3:15);

verse.he: וּבְנֵי יֹאשִׁיָּהוּ הַבְּכוֹר יוֹחָנָן הַשֵּׁנִי יְהוֹיָקִים הַשְּׁלִשִׁי צִדְקִיָּהוּ הָרְבִיעִי שַׁלּוּם׃
verse.en: The sons of Josiah: Johanan the first-born, the second Jehoiakim, the third Zedekiah, the fourth Shallum.

messages.text: The one who is called Johanan in that verse is also called Jehoahaz, and the one who is called Zedekiah is the same as the one called Shallum.

notes.he: ה"ג [ואמר רבי] יוחנן הוא יהואחז צדקיהו הוא שלום:
notes.en: This is the reading: [And Rabbi] Yoḥanan said: He is Jehoahaz; Zedekiah is Shallum.

messages.text: If so, Jehoahaz is the eldest son, not Jehoiakim. Why, then, was it necessary to anoint Jehoahaz?

notes.he: אלא יהואחז קשיש מדקרי ליה בכור:
notes.en: Rather, Jehoahaz was older, since it calls him firstborn.

messages.text: Rather, Jehoiakim was actually older than Jehoahaz. And why does the verse call Jehoahaz the firstborn? This is referring to the fact that Jehoahaz was the firstborn with regard to the monarchy, i.e., he became king first.

notes.he: לא להכי קרי ליה בכור שהוא בכור למלכות שמלך קודם אחיו:
notes.en: No, it calls him firstborn for this reason: that he is firstborn to the kingship, since he reigned before his brother.

messages.text: And do we establish the younger son as king before the older son? But isn’t it written with regard to Jehoshaphat: “And he gave the kingdom to Jehoram, because he was the firstborn” (II Chronicles 21:3)?

verse.he: וַיִּתֵּן לָהֶם ׀ אֲבִיהֶם מַתָּנוֹת רַבּוֹת לְכֶסֶף וּלְזָהָב וּלְמִגְדָּנוֹת עִם־עָרֵי מְצֻרוֹת בִּיהוּדָה וְאֶת־הַמַּמְלָכָה נָתַן לִיהוֹרָם כִּי־הוּא הַבְּכוֹר׃ {פ}
verse.en: Their father gave them many gifts of silver, gold, and [other] presents, as well as fortified towns in Judah, but he gave the kingdom to Jehoram because he was the first-born.

messages.text: Jehoram was one who filled the place of his fathers, i.e., he was fit to serve as king, and therefore as he was firstborn he received the kingship, whereas Jehoiakim was deemed unworthy of the honor, despite being the oldest among his brothers.

notes.he: ואע"פ שרשע הוא שמא באותו שעה הוי צדיק:
notes.en: He filled the place of his fathers: and although he was wicked, perhaps at that time he was righteous.

messages.text: The one who is called Shallum is also called Zedekiah. The Gemara objects: But the Torah counts these individuals in a row, i.e., one after the other, as I Chronicles 3:15 mentions the first, second, third, and fourth sons. This indicates that they are different people.
messages.quote: Zedekiah is the same as the one called Shallum

notes.he: דחשיב שלישי ורביעי:
notes.en: But it counts them in a row: since it counts third and fourth.

notes.he: כלומר שלישי והדר רביעי שהוא רביעי למלכות:
notes.en: But it counts them in a row: that is, third and then fourth; for he is fourth to the kingship.

messages.text: Shallum and Zedekiah are in fact one and the same, and what is the reason the verse calls Zedekiah the third? The reason is that he is third of the sons, i.e., the third in order of birth. And what is the reason the verse calls Shallum the fourth? The reason is that he is fourth to the kingship, because Jeconiah reigned before him.

notes.he: בן יהויקים תחת יהויקים אביו קמי צדקיהו:
notes.en: Because Jeconiah reigned: the son of Jehoiakim, in place of Jehoiakim his father, before Zedekiah.

messages.text: How so? Initially Jehoahaz reigned, and afterward Jehoiakim reigned, and afterward Jeconiah reigned, and afterward Zedekiah reigned. Accordingly, Zedekiah, called Shallum, was fourth to the kingship.

notes.he: ויצא בגלות וגלותו עמו קודם חרבן וסוף מלך צדקיהו:
notes.en: Because Jeconiah [the text calls him “ben dodo”] reigned before him, and he went into exile, and his exiles with him, before the destruction; and in the end Zedekiah reigned.

messages.caption: The sons of Josiah as I Chronicles 3:15 lists them, and the order in which they reigned, as the Gemara explains the verse.

messages.text: The one who is called Shallum is also called Zedekiah, and why was he called Shallum? Because he was perfect [shalem] in his good deeds. Alternatively, he was called Shallum because in his days the kingdom of the house of David was completed [shalam], as he was the last king in the Davidic dynasty.

And what was his true name? Mattaniah was his name, as it is stated: “And the king of Babylonia made Mattaniah, his father’s brother, king in his stead, and changed his name to Zedekiah” (II Kings 24:17).

verse.he: וַיַּמְלֵךְ מֶלֶךְ־בָּבֶל אֶת־מַתַּנְיָה דֹדוֹ תַּחְתָּיו וַיַּסֵּב אֶת־שְׁמוֹ צִדְקִיָּהוּ׃ {פ}
verse.en: And the king of Babylon appointed Mattaniah, Jehoiachin’s uncle, king in his place, changing his name to Zedekiah.

messages.text: Why did the king of Babylonia, Nebuchadnezzar, call him by the name Zedekiah? The reason is that Nebuchadnezzar said to him: God will justify [yatzdik] the judgment over you if you rebel against me, as it is stated with regard to Nebuchadnezzar and Jehoiachin: “And brought him to Babylon” (II Chronicles 36:10), and with regard to Zedekiah it is stated: “And he also rebelled against King Nebuchadnezzar, who had made him swear by God” (II Chronicles 36:13).

verse.he: וְגַם בַּמֶּלֶךְ נְבוּכַדְנֶאצַּר מָרָד אֲשֶׁר הִשְׁבִּיעוֹ בֵּאלֹהִים וַיֶּקֶשׁ אֶת־עׇרְפּוֹ וַיְאַמֵּץ אֶת־לְבָבוֹ מִשּׁוּב אֶל־יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל׃
verse.en: He also rebelled against Nebuchadnezzar, who made him take an oath by God; he stiffened his neck and hardened his heart so as not to turn to the ETERNAL God of Israel.

messages.text: § And was there anointing oil in the days of Jehoahaz? But isn’t it taught in a baraita:
messages.quote: And Jehoahaz, son of Josiah, was anointed

notes.he: בימי יהואחז והא נגנז בימי יאשיה אביו דתניא משנגנז ארון כו':
notes.en: And was there anointing oil in the days of Jehoahaz? But it was sequestered in the days of Josiah his father, as it is taught: From when the Ark was sequestered, etc.

messages.text: From when the Ark was sequestered, along with it was sequestered the jar of manna that was next to it (see Exodus 16:33), and the flask of the anointing oil, and Aaron’s staff with its almonds and blossoms (see Numbers 17:23),

And also sequestered with the Ark was the chest that the Philistines sent as a gift to the God of Israel after they captured the Ark and were stricken by several plagues, as it is stated: “And put the jewels of gold that you return to Him for a guilt offering, in a coffer by its side, and send it away that it may go” (I Samuel 6:8).

verse.he: וּלְקַחְתֶּם אֶת־אֲרוֹן יְהֹוָה וּנְתַתֶּם אֹתוֹ אֶל־הָעֲגָלָה וְאֵת ׀ כְּלֵי הַזָּהָב אֲשֶׁר הֲשֵׁבֹתֶם לוֹ אָשָׁם תָּשִׂימוּ בָאַרְגַּז מִצִּדּוֹ וְשִׁלַּחְתֶּם אֹתוֹ וְהָלָךְ׃
