verse.en: Take the Ark of GOD and place it on the cart; and put next to it in a chest the gold objects you are paying as indemnity. Send it off, and let it go its own way.

notes.he: מדכתיב בארגז מצדו אלמא כל היכא דהוי ארון הוי ארגז בהדיה וכי איגניז איגניז בהדיה:
notes.en: As it is stated, “And the vessels of gold,” etc.: since it is written “in a coffer by its side,” evidently wherever the Ark was, the coffer was with it, and when [the Ark] was sequestered, it was sequestered with it.

notes.he: כלומר שנגנז בצד הארון:
notes.en: “You shall put in a coffer by its side”: that is, that it was sequestered by the side of the Ark.

messages.text: And who sequestered the Ark? Josiah, king of Judah, sequestered it, as it is stated: And the king said to the priests: Put the sacred Ark in the house that Solomon, the son of David, king of Israel, built (see II Chronicles 35:3).

notes.he: בבית אשר בנה שלמה כי אין לכם משא בכתף וגרסינן במסכת שקלים (פ"ו ה"א) אמר להם אם גלה עמכם לבבל שוב אין אתם מחזירין אותו בכתפיכם וגנזו:
notes.en: Put the Ark: in the house that Solomon built; it shall no longer be a burden on your shoulders [II Chronicles 35:3]. And we read in Tractate Shekalim (6:1): He said to them: If it goes into exile with you to Babylonia, you will no longer bring it back on your shoulders; and he sequestered it.

messages.text: How do we know that all these items needed to be sequestered together with the Ark? The halakha that the jar of manna was to be kept with the Ark is derived through a verbal analogy between the words “there” and “there.” The word “there” is stated with regard to the Ark: “Where I will meet with you there” (Exodus 30:6), and it is also stated with regard to the manna: “And put there” (Exodus 16:33).

verse.he: וַיֹּאמֶר מֹשֶׁה אֶל־אַהֲרֹן קַח צִנְצֶנֶת אַחַת וְתֶן־שָׁמָּה מְלֹא־הָעֹמֶר מָן וְהַנַּח אֹתוֹ לִפְנֵי יְהֹוָה לְמִשְׁמֶרֶת לְדֹרֹתֵיכֶם׃
verse.en: And Moses said to Aaron, “Take a jar, put one omer of manna in it, and place it before GOD, to be kept throughout the ages.”

notes.he: כתיב בארון (שמות ל׳:ו׳) אשר אועד לך שמה ובצנצנת כתיב (שם טז) ותן שמה מלא העומר מן:
notes.en: The jar: derived from “there” and “there.” It is written concerning the Ark (Exodus 30:6): “Where I will meet with you there,” and concerning the jar it is written (ibid. 16[:33]): “And put there an omer-full of manna.”

notes.he: צנצנת המן דנגנז אתיא שמה שמה כתיב הכא ותן שמה מלא העומר מן וכתיב בארון ונועדתי לך שם וכתיב בצנצנת משמרת וכתיב במקלו של אהרן למשמרת לאות לבני מרי:
notes.en: And Rabbi Elazar said: the jar of manna that was sequestered is derived from “there” and “there.” Here it is written, “And put there an omer-full of manna,” and concerning the Ark it is written, “And I will meet with you there.” And concerning the jar, “to be kept” is written, and concerning Aaron’s staff: “to be kept for a sign against the rebellious children.”

messages.text: The halakha that the anointing oil was to be kept together with the Ark is derived through a verbal analogy between the words “generations” and “generations.” This term is stated with regard to the jar of manna: “To be kept throughout your generations” (Exodus 16:33), and also with regard to the anointing oil: “This shall be a sacred anointing oil to Me throughout your generations” (Exodus 30:31).

notes.he: מצנצנת:
notes.en: And the anointing oil: derived from “generations” and “generations,” from the jar.

notes.he: כתיב בצנצנת למשמרת לדורותיכם וכתיב בשמן המשחה זה לי לדורותיכם מלמד (שכולו) [שכולן] נגנזו:
notes.en: And it is derived from “generations” and “generations”: concerning the jar it is written, “to be kept throughout your generations,” and concerning the anointing oil: “This shall be to Me throughout your generations.” This teaches that all of them were sequestered.

messages.text: Finally, the halakha that Aaron’s staff was to be kept together with the Ark is derived through a verbal analogy between the terms “to be kept” and “to be kept.” This term is stated with regard to the jar of manna, and also with regard to Aaron’s staff: “To be kept there, for a token against the rebellious children” (Numbers 17:25).

verse.he: וַיֹּאמֶר יְהֹוָה אֶל־מֹשֶׁה הָשֵׁב אֶת־מַטֵּה אַהֲרֹן לִפְנֵי הָעֵדוּת לְמִשְׁמֶרֶת לְאוֹת לִבְנֵי־מֶרִי וּתְכַל תְּלוּנֹּתָם מֵעָלַי וְלֹא יָמֻתוּ׃
verse.en: GOD said to Moses, “Put Aaron’s staff back before the Pact, to be kept as a lesson to rebels, so that their mutterings against Me may cease, lest they die.”

notes.dh: מקלו של אהרן אתיא משמרת משמרת
notes.he: מצנצנת. כתיב במקל (במדבר י״ז:כ״ה) למשמרת לאות לבני מרי בצנצנת למשמרת לדורותיכם:
notes.en: Aaron’s staff: derived from “to be kept” and “to be kept,” from the jar. It is written of the staff (Numbers 17:25): “to be kept for a sign against the rebellious children,” and of the jar: “to be kept throughout your generations.”

messages.text: All these items, which are connected through these verbal analogies, including the anointing oil, were kept by the side of the Ark, and therefore they were sequestered together with the Ark. If so, how was Jehoahaz anointed with the anointing oil?
They did not anoint Jehoahaz with the anointing oil, but with pure balsam.
One anoints the kings by placing the oil around the head in a shape similar to a crown, and one anoints the High Priests by placing the oil upon the head in the shape similar to chi.

notes.he: סביב על ראשו:
notes.en: Like a crown: around his head.

notes.he: משחו במצחו מאוזן לאוזן וערפו אחוריו כלומר סביב סביב כמין כי יווני ח כך מן המצח על גבי הראש עד העורף ומפרש כמין כי:
notes.en: Like a crown: they anointed him on his forehead from ear to ear and at the back of his neck behind him, that is, all around. Like a Greek chi [the printed text shows the Hebrew letter ח here]: thus, from the forehead over the head to the back of the neck. [Editor’s note: see what is written in Arukh HaShalem, entry “ki” 1, which explains “like a chi.”]

messages.text: It is placed in a shape similar to the Greek letter chi, which looks like the letter Χ.

notes.he: אות יוונית ועשוי כזה x דמציק שמן על ראשו ואח"כ בין ריסי עיניו ומצרפן באצבעו דרך הפדחת:
notes.en: Like a chi: a Greek letter, made like this: X. For he pours oil on his head and afterward [puts oil] between his eyelashes, and joins them with his finger by way of the forehead.

messages.text: First, one pours oil on the head of the High Priest, and afterward one places oil between his eyelashes.
First, one places oil between his eyelashes, and afterward one pours oil on his head.
The baraitot contradict each other.

This is a matter of dispute between tanna’im, as there is a tanna who says: Anointing between his eyelashes is preferable to pouring on the head and therefore comes first, and there is a tanna who says that pouring on the head is preferable to anointing between his eyelashes, and therefore comes first.

What is the reasoning of the one who says that pouring on the head is preferable? As it is stated: “And he poured of the anointing oil upon Aaron’s head and anointed him to sanctify him” (Leviticus 8:12), which indicates that pouring is first, followed by anointing.

verse.he: וַיִּצֹק מִשֶּׁמֶן הַמִּשְׁחָה עַל רֹאשׁ אַהֲרֹן וַיִּמְשַׁח אֹתוֹ לְקַדְּשׁוֹ׃
verse.en: He poured some of the anointing oil upon Aaron’s head and anointed him, to consecrate him.

messages.text: And as for the one who says that anointing between his eyelashes is preferable to pouring on the head and precedes it, he holds that anointing is preferable in that its use is increased, i.e., it is performed on the service vessels, whereas pouring is not mentioned with regard to the service vessels.

notes.he: תני חדא כו' מאן דאמר תחלה בין ריסי עיניו מושח קסבר משיחה עדיפא שכן נתרבתה אצל כלי שרת. שלא מצינו בהן יציקה אלא משיחה:
notes.en: It is taught in one [baraita], etc. The one who says that he first anoints between his eyelashes holds that anointing is preferable, since it was increased with regard to the service vessels, for we do not find pouring with them, only anointing.

messages.text: The Gemara raises a difficulty: But according to the opinion that anointing is preferable, isn’t it written: “He poured,” and ultimately: “He anointed” (Leviticus 8:12)? The Gemara explains that this is what the verse is saying: What is the reason for “he poured”? This action was made possible due to the fact that he had already: “Anointed him to sanctify him.” In other words, the pouring came after the anointing, which is the primary act.

notes.he: כבר:
notes.en: Because of “and he anointed him to sanctify him”: already.

messages.text: The verse states: “It is like the precious oil upon the head descending upon the beard; the beard of Aaron, that descends upon the collar of his garments” (Psalms 133:2). Two drops of anointing oil shaped like pearls hung from Aaron’s beard.

verse.he: כַּשֶּׁמֶן הַטּוֹב ׀ עַל־הָרֹאשׁ יֹרֵד עַל־הַזָּקָן זְקַן־אַהֲרֹן שֶׁיֹּרֵד עַל־פִּי מִדּוֹתָיו׃
verse.en:
It is like fine oil on the head
running down onto the beard,
the beard of Aaron,
that comes down over the collar of his robe;

messages.text: When Aaron would speak his beard would move, and these drops would miraculously rise and sit on the roots of his beard, so that they would not fall to the ground.

notes.he: מדבר. ל"א מסתפר דשקיל במזייה:
notes.en: Mesaper: speaks. Another version: mistaper, has his hair cut, when he cuts his hair.

notes.he: מדבר עולות ויושבות לו בעיקרי זקנו. כדי שלא יפלו לארץ כשהוא מנענע פיו לדבר:
notes.en: When he would speak [mesaper]: they would rise and sit for him on the roots of his beard, so that they would not fall to the ground when he moved his mouth to speak.

messages.text: And with regard to this matter Moses, our teacher, was concerned, thinking: Perhaps, God forbid, I misused the anointing oil by pouring too much, which resulted in these two additional drops.

notes.he: ששמתי שם יותר מדאי:
notes.en: Perhaps I misused: by putting too much there.

notes.he: ועל דבר זה היה משה דואג שהיה משה (אמר) [אומר] שמא מעלתי לפי שהזקן לא נצטוה למשוח והיה רואה בו ב' טיפין מן הראש ירדו לזקן:
notes.en: And concerning this matter Moses was worried, for Moses would say: perhaps I misused, since [the oil] was not commanded for anointing the beard, and he would see on it two drops that had gone down from the head to the beard.

messages.text: A Divine Voice emerged and said: “It is like the precious oil upon the head, descending upon the beard; the beard of Aaron, that descends upon the collar of his garments, like the dew of the Hermon that comes down upon the mountains of Zion” (Psalms 133:2–3). This comparison serves to teach: Just as the Hermon’s dew is not subject to misuse of consecrated property, as it is not consecrated but can be used by all, so too, the anointing oil that descends upon Aaron’s beard is not subject to misuse of consecrated property.

verse.he: כְּטַל־חֶרְמוֹן שֶׁיֹּרֵד עַל־הַרְרֵי צִיּוֹן כִּי שָׁם ׀ צִוָּה יְהֹוָה אֶת־הַבְּרָכָה חַיִּים עַד־הָעוֹלָם׃ {פ}
verse.en:
like the dew of Hermon
that falls upon the mountains of Zion.
There GOD ordained blessing,
everlasting life.

messages.text: And still Aaron himself was concerned, thinking: Perhaps Moses did not misuse consecrated property but I misused the oil, as the additional oil is on my body and I derive benefit from it.

notes.he: שבגדי נהנים מריח השמן שבזקני:
notes.en: And I misused: since my garments benefit from the fragrance of the oil in my beard.

notes.he: שמא אני מעלתי שאני נהנה בריח שבזקני יצאה ב"ק כו':
notes.en: A Divine Voice emerged, etc. [Aaron said:] Perhaps I misused, since I benefit from the fragrance that is in my beard. A Divine Voice emerged, etc.

messages.text: A Divine Voice emerged and said to him: “Behold how good and how pleasant it is for brothers to dwell together in unity” (Psalms 133:1). Just as your brother Moses did not misuse consecrated property, so too, you did not misuse consecrated property.

verse.he: שִׁיר הַמַּעֲלוֹת לְדָוִד הִנֵּה מַה־טּוֹב וּמַה־נָּעִים שֶׁבֶת אַחִים גַּם־יָחַד׃
verse.en:
A song of ascents. Of David.
How good and how pleasant it is
that kindred dwell together.

messages.text: One may anoint kings only next to a spring. This is done as a fortuitous sign, so that their kingdom should continue uninterrupted just as the waters of the spring flow uninterrupted throughout the year.
messages.lead: § The Gemara cites a baraita which discusses the anointing of kings. The Sages taught:

notes.he: מעיין קטן סמוך לירושלים ולא זהו גיחון הגדול היוצא מעדן:
notes.en: Gihon: a small spring near Jerusalem, and not the great Gihon that goes out of Eden.

messages.text: As it is stated with regard to the coronation of Solomon in the days of King David: And the king said to Benaiah: Take with you the servants of your lord, and cause Solomon my son to ride upon my own mule, and bring him down to Gihon. And let Zadok the priest and Nathan the prophet anoint him there king over Israel (see I Kings 1:33–34). The Sages derived from here that all kings should be anointed near a spring.

verse.he: וַיֹּאמֶר הַמֶּלֶךְ לָהֶם קְחוּ עִמָּכֶם אֶת־עַבְדֵי אֲדֹנֵיכֶם וְהִרְכַּבְתֶּם אֶת־שְׁלֹמֹה בְנִי עַל־הַפִּרְדָּה אֲשֶׁר־לִי וְהוֹרַדְתֶּם אֹתוֹ אֶל־גִּחוֹן׃ וּמָשַׁח אֹתוֹ שָׁם צָדוֹק הַכֹּהֵן וְנָתָן הַנָּבִיא לְמֶלֶךְ עַל־יִשְׂרָאֵל וּתְקַעְתֶּם בַּשּׁוֹפָר וַאֲמַרְתֶּם יְחִי הַמֶּלֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹה׃
verse.en: the king said to them, “Take my loyal soldiers, and have my son Solomon ride on my mule and bring him down to Gihon. Let the priest Zadok and the prophet Nathan anoint him there king over Israel, whereupon you shall sound the horn and shout, ‘Long live King Solomon!’

messages.text: One who desires to know if he will live through this current year or not should bring a lit candle during those ten days between Rosh HaShana and Yom Kippur and hang it in a house through which wind does not blow, and he should watch it carefully: If its light continues he shall know that he will live out his year.
messages.lead: Parenthetical to this matter of performing an act as a fortuitous sign, the Gemara cites that which

notes.he: עד שיכלה כל השמן שבכלי:
notes.en: If its light continues: until all the oil in the vessel is used up.

messages.text: And one who desires to conduct business and wants to know if his business will succeed or not should raise a rooster. If the rooster gets fat and beautiful he shall know that the venture will succeed.

notes.he: לשם כך:
notes.en: Should raise a hen [Rashi reads tarnegolta, a hen; the printed text reads tarnegola, a rooster]: for this purpose.

notes.he: על שם אותו עסקא:
notes.en: Should raise a hen [Rabbeinu Gershom reads tarnegolta, a hen]: in the name of that venture.

messages.text: This one who wishes to leave on a journey and wants to know whether he will return to his home should enter a dark house. If he sees …

notes.he: אפל במקצת:
notes.en: In a dark house [beveita debahata]: somewhat dark.

messages.text: Continues on 6a: what he must see in the dark house, and the warning that one should not rely on such signs.
